rows.text: Hold on, I... I'll be there soon.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What did I tell you, [Trailblazer]? He's definitely sleeping in.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We Trailblazers can go days without sleep, but when we do hit the hay, we have to make up for it. Anyway, no point wasting our time in the corridor.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hands out!
Arms by my side!
Wait, what am I supposed to do!?
The conductor wants us to attend a warp navigation meeting. Same old location apparently, and we can't be late~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's head over. Oh, by the way...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You drew the short straw, [Trailblazer]. It's your turn to wash the coffee cups this week.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Morning, [Trailblazer]. You're very punctual.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And a wonderful morning to you, Himeko.
Punctual is my middle name.
I'm reporting Dan Heng for—
*sigh* I can't remember the last time I got such a polite response.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Well hang onto it, it's cute.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Ah, no need to worry, Dan Heng's rarely late. I'm sure he must have a good reason...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Dan Heng's situation is special — we hope to protect him to the best of our ability.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The trailblazing of Jarilo-VI has drawn to a close, and the Astral Express must depart for the next planet.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: What's the next planet like?
Trailblazing really is a full-time job, huh.
Any chance for a little break first?
Not telling yet... We'll make an official announcement in the meeting, but I'm keeping you in suspense for now~
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The universe is boundless, and trailblazing never ends... Even a lifetime isn't enough to explore every world. That's the beauty of the unknown.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: That hardly sounds like you, [Trailblazer]. What about that Stellaron inside you? Don't you wanna get rid of it?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The meeting will start soon.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: See, it's like I said: If you wake up and Dan Heng's not around, then you probably won't see him the rest of the day either.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Didn't Himeko say not to worry?
Dan Heng sure is a mysterious guy.
How shocking...
I guess. To be honest, warp navigation meetings are basically just like that "teambuilding" you're always going on about. You don't have to show up, but Himeko might be upset if you don't.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Think about it, Dan Heng's the one managing the archives — he'll already be clued in to our next destination. Himeko and Welt know already, of course... so it's just me and you in the dark!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah... I heard he did something incredible once, and now some powerful force has his name on a wanted list. My guess is the Xianzhou Alliance or the Garden of Recollection. In any case, it can't be the IPC — I've seen their wanted list.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmm... I bet it is the Garden of Recollection. Didn't it seem like Dan Heng was super keen on talking to Herta? Everyone knows that Herta and the Garden of Recollection don't get along. They say the enemy of your enemy is your friend...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ha! Shocking? I guess you're still new — you'll find out how strange everyone is around here sooner or later...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What's with the funny look? Am I not strange enough for you? Name me an amnesiac that didn't have some crazy backstory. I already made up a few dozen for myself.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You're looking well, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You coming with us this time?
Do you know what our next destination is?
What world do you want to go to?
Haha, you better believe it. You guys really put on a show for Jarilo-VI — I'm eager to join in myself.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I gotta say, there were more than a few times where I wanted to lend a hand... but Himeko said I should let you youngsters rise to the trailblazing challenges...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I know alright, but I can't tell you yet. Himeko wants to create a sense of mystery for you and March.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That I want to go to? ...My home world, I suppose. Sadly, its location doesn't appear on the Express' astral chart records, at least the ones that are undamaged.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: In any case, I do want to see some other civilizations before I go home. It'd be a crime to waste this opportunity on the Express.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ahem... [Trailblazer], did you receive the destination overview? Excited?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Himeko's going to announce it in the meeting.
We got it.
So you don't know yet...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: You don't seem very excited...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: After all that cold and exhaustion on Jarilo-VI, you must be looking forward to the next planet!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: ...It's simple. That Stellaron has nothing to do with us, but the Xianzhou is convinced that we're responsible.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Pom-Pom's thrilled that you're enjoying your journey!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: A long, long time ago, this train would ferry the Nameless from planet to planet... Now it's able to do the same again.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Pegana? That's the final stop — Akivili's home world... Pom-Pom wants to visit again too. Unfortunately, the journey's a lot like life — you don't always get where you're going right away.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: ...There are some planets that haven't been affected by Stellarons.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: The Express moves at an incredible speed, but change is always faster...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: [Trailblazer], if you're ready, head over to the front of the train. The meeting is about to start!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Passengers! The warp navigation meeting has officially begun!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Firstly, Pom-Pom wants to congratulate you, the Nameless, for successfully resolving the problems at this stop. The Express is now able to continue along the star rail!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: The three of us actually pulled it off, huh [Trailblazer]!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's time for your conductor — ahem, that's me — to reveal the name of our next stop...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: I've seen your face before, Stellaron Hunter, even if it was only on a Corporation wanted poster. They were offering quite the bounty... dead or alive. Do you know the figure?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Doesn't concern me. Then again, a Corporation bounty is a compliment, not an insult, don't you think? The higher the figure, the bigger the compliment.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: You wanted criminals sure know how to look on the bright side of things...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...I will say, Herta certainly paid you all a compliment: "A {RUBY_B#Elio}maniac{RUBY_E#} that claims he can see destiny, leading a bunch of {RUBY_B#Stellaron Hunters}wild lunatics{RUBY_E#} in pursuit of the most dangerous objects in the universe!" ...And Herta doesn't give out compliments very often.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In pursuit of the most dangerous objects in the universe, huh? ...In that sense, you Astral Expressers and I are cut from the same cloth.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: You're in the wrong place, Kafka. We're not about to accept your request, and we're not about to get into bed with a Stellaron Hunter. It was nice talking with you. Perhaps next time you'll be willing to pay us a visit in person and we can continue our little discussion.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Have you guys heard of the Luofu?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...The Xianzhou Luofu? It belongs to the Hexafleet of the Xianzhou Alliance. We've heard of it.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mm. But what you haven't heard is that it's currently very close to you — a couple of warp jumps away, in fact.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Not to mention, 45 system hours ago... a Stellaron burst occurred on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: An unexpected calamity... don't you think?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What exactly are you Stellaron Hunters trying to do...? The Xianzhou Alliance aren't us — they won't give you time to explain. Once you draw the attention of {RUBY_B#Lan}The Hunt{RUBY_E#}, you become their prey. The Alliance will hunt you to the end of the universe...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Three against two. Well, it looks like the Astral Express crew has a majority vote to head for the Xianzhou!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Three against two. Well, it looks like the Astral Express crew has a majority vote to head for the Xianzhou!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Stop speaking in riddles, Kafka. Say what you have to say.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: My companion Blade has been taken away by the Cloud Knights. I want to bring him back, resolve this Stellaron crisis, and clear our names.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Nothing to do with you? Yeah right — sounds like a weird coincidence to me. You just happened to show up after the Stellaron burst...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Also, we're not your friends. Why should we care if a Stellaron Hunter is innocent, hmm~?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We should seal the Stellaron and help the Xianzhou.
Maybe we can sell our friendship to the Stellaron Hunters.
Is there anything in this for us?

No! Why are we listening to her? The Alliance is strong — is a single Stellaron burst really too much for them to handle? We're the crew of the Astral Express, not some squad of Stellaron-sealing super specialists!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You could, of course, not get involved. Knowing that the Stellaron hasn't yet affected this region of space, you could make the jump and arrive at the next world. But sooner or later, the star rail here will be more blocked off than it was before.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I can tell you what the future holds: If you don't go to the Luofu, the Stellaron will eventually contaminate the entire ship, and over half of the inhabitants will perish.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Oh you brave and fearless Trailblazers, you benevolent Nameless, can you really remain indifferent to that?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...This companion of yours, Blade, he'd perish too, right?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: No comment.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Here are the coordinates. It's up to you how to proceed.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Please await transfer... Please await transfer... Please await transfer...
rows.speaker: Intermittent Signal

rows.text: Our destinations may differ, but the orbits of the stars will eventually converge. See you later.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...March, get Dan Heng.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Kafka... *sigh* Pom-Pom doesn't like her. She smells of danger.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Still, a Trailblazer should choose their goal and the road they take to get there themselves. That's the creed of the great Akivili.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: How could the mighty Xianzhou Alliance be breached by a Stellaron...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Something's not right. The Xianzhou Alliance is a small faction, but one that derives its power directly from an Aeon. They have immense strength — much more than a train under the protection of the fallen Akivili.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Please await transfer... Please await transfer... Please await transfer...
rows.speaker: Intermittent Signal

rows.text: Stellarons can lead to the collapse of stars scattered throughout the universe, but the Xianzhou has Lan, The Hunt on their side. I struggle to believe that Stellarons pose a threat in the eyes of the Aeons.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Either the Stellaron Hunters are lying, or... there's an even bigger threat lurking on the Xianzhou Luofu...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's fair to say that it ranks highly among the known forces in the universe.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Path of The Hunt is narrow and doesn't stand out among the other Paths, but the Alliance enjoys the direct blessing of the Aeon. The six great ships of the Xianzhou are like brothers in arms.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Its power is much greater than those factions that simply draw their strength from the Paths themselves.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I want to hear your thoughts.
I want to know more about the Xianzhou Alliance.
Are you allowed to divulge our original destination...?
I won't disturb you.
Something's not right — the Xianzhou has Lan The Hunt's blessing. I struggle to believe that Stellarons pose a threat in the eyes of the Aeons...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Which means either the Stellaron Hunters are lying, or... there's an even bigger threat lurking on the Xianzhou Luofu.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Alliance is made up of six great ships, all following Lan, The Hunt. Its mission is to eliminate the Aeon of Abundance.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Lan doesn't rank among the more powerful Aeons — the concept of the Path of The Hunt is narrow... but in contrast with the other Aeons, THEY pay close attention to mortals. Lan grants strength to the Xianzhou Alliance without reservation.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It follows that the Alliance's Marshal and six Generals are in no way inferior to Lord Ravagers.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I guess it doesn't matter if I tell you now... Our original destination was a place called Penacony. The records on the Express indicate that it's a prison planet used by the IPC to exile criminals — at least that's how it was in the days of Akivili.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: When the Cancer of All Worlds broke out, the IPC lost control of Penacony, and the planet sought refuge under Xipe the Harmony. Now it's a member of "The Family."
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Penacony is holding an event, and The Family sent an invitation to the Express. Himeko intends to accept the invitation, so we were planning to travel there as guests, not Trailblazers.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...But alas, for now we're changing our bearings and heading for the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: [Trailblazer], what do you think about all this?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh? And why is that?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We can't trust everything Kafka says. It's credible that the leader of the Stellaron Hunters can predict the future, but Kafka might not be telling the truth.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Oh? How come?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You're right. It's credible that the leader of the Stellaron Hunters can predict the future, but Kafka might not be telling the truth.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It wouldn't be surprising. I've seen the IPC's file on Blade. If the details are accurate, he's incredibly dangerous.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's hard to believe that someone like him could be captured by the Cloud Knights and that the Stellaron Hunters would look to us for help.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yes, however... if she is telling the truth and we turn a deaf ear, then those on the Luofu will be in great danger.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I like the way you think.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: [Trailblazer], did you notice that Kafka didn't mention anything to do with you...?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Maybe Blade's more important.
I have nothing to do with her anymore.
(I wonder if she even remembers we've got a job to do down there...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It seemed like she was avoiding it.
(I wonder if she even remembers we've got a job to do down there...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A Stellaron Hunter implanted you with a Stellaron — a move like that hints at a far-off purpose. Everyone says that Elio can foresee the future, and that every step of his schemes is a foreshadowing.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: (I wonder if she even remembers we've got a job to do down there...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You must be extra vigilant, [Trailblazer]. Kafka won't always turn a blind eye.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So Welt's got skills?
I knew there was more to him than meets the eye...
Don't worry, I'll take care of March and him.
Whoa, what are you doing here?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...But that's only a small part of his story. Believe me when I say he has more experience than I do.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I just gave him the low-down. Hey, remember what I said, okay? We're gonna vote against it! I'm not gonna take orders from that woman.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...But that's only a small part of his story. Believe me when I say he has more experience than I do.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's waaaay too much of a coincidence. A Stellaron Hunter shows up at the site of a Stellaron burst that just happens to be occurring nearby. Does anyone really believe that?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm so mad! She just hijacks our communications and then hangs up? So rude! [Trailblazer], you used to know her, right? Was she always like this?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...We don't need another amnesiac on this train...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh yeah? Huh, maybe she really liked you...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh yeah, I just spoke to Dan Heng, here's the deal: We've all gotta vote against!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Doesn't Himeko have the final say?
I want to vote in favor.
Trust me, she'll hold a democratic vote. One for you, one for me, one for Dan Heng — three altogether. We never go anywhere without a consensus.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph, I should've known you'd listen to that Stellaron Hunter. Whatever — but you should think before you do that.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Seems like the longer I spend in my room, the stranger things are when I emerge.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We might be going to the Xianzhou Luofu.
Mm, March told me... *sigh* If it were one of the other ships it might've been okay, but I can't go to the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So you and the Luofu have history?
Other ships? Which ones?
I don't remember.
She used to be nice.
{M#A man should keep his past a secret.}{F#You shouldn't talk about girls behind their backs.}
Well, that's up to you.
I'm forbidden from setting foot on that ship. "Total interception of any attempt to enter the dominion" is how they chose to put it. *sigh*
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Pfft, taking things seriously all of a sudden...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...So if you're planning on going, I can't go with you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Alliance is made up of six ships — the Luofu is only one of them.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There are also the Yaoqing, the Fanghu, the Zhuming, the Xuling, and the Yuque.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I remember the Xianzhou was a sight to behold. Good luck.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Are you okay, Dan Heng? March brought you up to speed, I assume?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'm fine, and yes, I'm up to speed.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Good. In that case, with regard to the matter at hand, let's vote to decide our next move.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: This is big. I'm coming with you this time.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Our Stellaron Hunter claims that a Stellaron burst has occurred on the Xianzhou Luofu, and that we're in the vicinity. If we head for the Luofu, we may have the chance to save many innocent lives.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...However, it's also possible that our Stellaron Hunter is lying and using us for her own ends. Neither Welt nor I believe that she's telling us the truth, but we can't just ignore the intel she's given us...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So, we're about to hold a democratic vote on whether to set a course for the Xianzhou. All those in favor, hold out your hand. All those against, keep your arms by your side.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Three, two, one...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Four against one. Well, it looks like the Astral Express crew has a majority vote to head for the Xianzhou!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Didn't you say you were voting against!?

*sigh* I calmed down and thought about it a bit. If it turns out that woman isn't lying, then a lot of innocent people are gonna get hurt... Now's the time for thinking about other people... hehe *sigh*
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, how suddenly principled of you!
You're so capricious!
Alright, alright, I think we're all used to March's modus operandi by now.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So, Dan Heng, you want to stay here?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Yes, I'm staying this time.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: In that case... Welt. Ready for a trailblazing expedition? I know you've been itching to get out there for a while now. But make sure you take good care of [Trailblazer] and March.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...Don't worry.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What do you make of it, Mr. Yang?
Is the Xianzhou Alliance really that powerful?
Destination Xianzhou, here we come!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Whoa! So that's a Xianzhou ship? It looks even bigger than Jarilo-VI!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: For Xianzhou natives, these ships are their planets.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Terrestrial environments are cradles that allow civilizations to survive and then develop. Some of those civilizations progress further — constructing space-faring vessels which allow them to voyage into the unknown... The Xianzhou Alliance is one such civilization.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I've only glimpsed it a few times, but... it's as magnificent as I remember...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You okay there? What's with all the lonely nostalgia vibes?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is big. I'm coming with you this time.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: This is the Astral Express, I repeat, this is the Astral Express. We have arrived in Xianzhou territory. Requesting landing permission from ground control... f—from the bridge, I mean.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Welcome to... Luofu skyport... Starskiff Haven...
rows.speaker: Intermittent Signal

rows.text: Is it stuck on repeat?
Sounds like one of those automated customer service numbers...
*sigh* Now you know how I feel when you copy me.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Something's not right.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The signal is still repeating, but no one is guiding us in to dock.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Maybe the Stellaron Hunters were telling the truth. It seems like something really did happen to the Xianzhou...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We should go to the Xianzhou.
We can't go to the Xianzhou.
I'm okay with whatever we do.
A vessel arrives at a deserted spaceport... Isn't that how, like, loads of horror movies start!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Because we're the Nameless.
Because the Xianzhou needs us.
Because we can't not go.
Haha, I see you're already a full-fledged Trailblazer. You're right, we can't remain indifferent to those in crisis.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Haha, I see you're already a full-fledged Trailblazer. You're right, we can't remain indifferent to those in crisis.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Let's not let our imaginations get the better of us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...This is a difficult matter. If she is telling the truth and we turn a deaf ear, then those on the Luofu will be in great danger.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Still the automated signal?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We can't trust what Kafka says.
The Stellaron Hunters are up to something.
This has nothing to do with us.
Yes, it's still on repeat... Ah! There we go.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...This is a difficult matter. If she is telling the truth and we turn a deaf ear, then those on the Luofu will be in great danger.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...The Jade Gate is now opening. On behalf of the Xianzhou Luofu: Welcome, guests from afar. Please proceed to dock in accordance with the guidance...
rows.speaker: Signal

rows.text: Huh? Is this still automated?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The signal broke off, seems that's all there is.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We should get going. Himeko, stay vigilant back here on the Express.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Relax, I've got Dan Heng here with me.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You're staying too?
I don't wanna go...
Trailblazers! Assemble~!
Yes, but I won't be putting my feet up. There's a lot to take care of here on the train.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Come onnnn, you were the most excited last time we got off the train!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I like all planets equally!
When will we get to Pegana?
Are these destination overviews still useful after a thousand years?
Make sure you're properly prepared before you set off.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Have a safe trip you guys!
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Pom-Pom's too busy — looking after the Express is a full-time job.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Never.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: (You can tell Pom-Pom's a little sad by looking at their ears.)
...Don't worry about me — I'm just happy you're enjoying the journey.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: (Pom-Pom still seems a little sad...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Allll this universe, and we just happen to bump into a Xianzhou ship that Dan Heng spent time on? That's gotta be fate! I wonder what Dan Heng stories await us.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That guy sure has a mysterious past. We gotta take this opportunity on the Luofu to dig into it!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Darn straight.
Give the man some privacy, please.
That might be dangerous...
I knew you'd be excited! Check out the master of gossip over here.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* Fine, you're right... In that case, we'll just have to take loads of selfies till he gets super jealous.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh? Is his past really that dark?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* Fine, I'll leave him alone then. We'll just have to take loads of selfies till he gets super jealous.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This time you'll get the chance to witness Welt in action, haha. I'm glad he's going with you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: He doesn't talk much about his past. If you ask him, he'll just tell you about how he worked in animation...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You could say he keeps his cards close to his chest. If you ask him, he'll just tell you about how he worked in animation...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Haha, much appreciated, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Before we set off, I need to clarify the aim of this journey with you...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Stellaron Hunters have given us a lot to consider, and a lot to doubt... But the most important part of this expedition is—
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Sampling the local delicacies.
Getting to know the people with power.
The Stellaron.
Always thinking with your stomach. What about all the scenic photo opportunities?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That Belobog expedition got in your head, huh...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At this point, I think it'd be creepier if we did see someone...
Ah! Stop talking! If there is someone here, they're in my bad books already.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yet someone opened the gate for us...
You're pretty decisive...
That's Mr. Yang — this is child's play for him. He's dealt with all kinds of dangers before.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What if they're not friendly and we can't defeat them...?
Are you forgetting we've got Mr. Yang with us? Oh, right, you haven't seen what he can do yet...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's move. Keep your wits about you.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Precisely.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Stellaron Hunters clearly have ulterior motives. However, knowing what they're all about and given the focus of Kafka's words, I have no doubt that the Xianzhou is dealing with a Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Alliance and the Express haven't had any previous dealings, so our arrival might not receive the warmest welcome. But as Trailblazers, we're not in this for fame or gain — we just need to do everything in our power to assist the Xianzhou and eliminate the source of disaster.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Always keep that in mind, and don't forget the way of the trailblaze: Explore, understand, establish, and connect.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yeahhhh~!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Let's go!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ugh, Look, it's just containers as far as the eye can see.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This area isn't for receiving guests, it's for unloading cargo! Who decided to send us this way?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Such a huge port and not a soul in sight. It gives me the creeps...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mr. Yang, what should we do?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We should start with the person who opened the Jade Gate. If it turns out they're not friendly, then at least they've already made things easier for us. If it turns out they were just doing their job, then we can ask them what happened here.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ugh, Look, it's just containers as far as the eye can see.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This area isn't for receiving guests, it's for unloading cargo! Who decided to send us this way?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Such a huge port and not a soul in sight. It gives me the creeps...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Leave it to me!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: At this point, I think it'd be creepier if we did see someone...
Yet someone opened the gate for us...
Ah! Stop talking! If there is someone here, they're in my bad books already.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mr. Yang, what should we do?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We should start with the person who opened the Jade Gate. If it turns out they're not friendly, then at least they've already made things easier for us. If it turns out they were just doing their job, then we can ask them what happened here.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You're pretty decisive...
What if they're not friendly and we can't defeat them...?
That's Mr. Yang — this is child's play for him. He's dealt with all kinds of dangers before.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are you forgetting we've got Mr. Yang with us? Oh, right, you haven't seen what he can do yet...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's move. Keep your wits about you.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mr. Yang, someone's hurt...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Up... Up ahead...
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: I'm [Trailblazer].
My name's a secret.
I'm... the Galactic Baseballer.
Trying to avoid ending up on another wanted list...
Best not to reveal our true names...
I'm just trying to avoid ending up on another wanted list.
Best to use a fake name...
You're hurt, son. Try not to talk.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: March, use your six-phased ice to stop the bleeding. Go easy, we don't wanna add frostbite to his list of complaints.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'm on it~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], March, this area saw fierce fighting only recently.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Let's keep searching, there might be other survivors.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: There are wounded everywhere...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The silver lining is that based on what we can see, no civilians were caught up in the battle...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'm guessing the Xianzhou must have evacuated the port immediately, leaving the soldiers to deal with the crisis. But as for these corroded monsters...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Careful, we've never seen this kind of life form before...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Awaiting orders, Mr. Yang!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss Tingyun! Fall back!
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: They're {RUBY_B#Long-Life Curse}mara-struck{RUBY_E#} — we've already lost them...
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Oh... hehe. {F#Miss}{M#Mr.} Secret.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Don't mind {F#her}{M#him}. {F#She}{M#He} likes to get a little creative with {F#her}{M#his} introductions.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Next time, why not remind me before I give up my name?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, you there! We need your help~!
Don't mind {F#her}{M#him}. {F#She}{M#He} likes to get a little creative with {F#her}{M#his} introductions.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Next time, why not remind me before I give up my name?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss Tingyun, the mara-struck have been repelled, b—but there could be other dangers nearby.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: The situation is serious. Allow us to escort you back to the Sky-Faring Commission, immediately.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Calm down, I heard you. It'd be rude of me to depart without thanking our benefactors.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: My name is Tingyun. I'm the Amicassador for the Luofu Sky-Faring Commission merchant guild. May I venture to know the illustrious names of my heroes?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Illustrious names? ...Uhh, sure. I'm March 7th, this is Mr. Yang — oh — Mr. Welt Yang, and this is—
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *chuckle* What a heroic-sounding name.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I see, well, thank you for coming to our aid. Although, there is one thing I don't understand: Starskiff Haven is under lockdown. Since none of you are Xianzhou residents, may I ask how you came to be here?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If you can't offer an explanation, I'm afraid these Cloud Knights will have to escort you out.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We called for port transfer and got no response, but then someone opened the Jade Gate for us. When we arrived there was no one to be found, so we started to make our own way through.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: How can that be? My ship was the last one into port before the Jade Gate was shut. The Sky-Faring Commission has already locked down Starskiff Haven entirely...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We're telling the truth. You could verify it yourself by checking the access history of the Jade Gate.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: W—We found it strange ourselves when the gate opened but no one came to greet us.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You're with... the Astral Express?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You've heard of us?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Indeed I have. *sigh* ...You've arrived at a bad time — the Xianzhou has suffered an incident. Whether you're here for leisure, treatment, or trade, I'm afraid you won't be able to go through with it.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: For your safety, you should hurry to Central Starskiff Haven and take refuge. I'll take you to Madam Yukong of the Sky-Faring Commission and let her decide how to proceed.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We caught wind of the incident you mention. That's why we're here Miss Tingyun — to help the Xianzhou seal the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hehe, your actions have already revealed your kind hearts to me! Sadly... I can't make you any promises. You're outsiders, and only Madam Yukong has the authority to consider your offer.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Don't worry! Madam Yukong is kind-hearted too. Come on now, I'll lead the way.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Those monsters back there...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'd like to see us try, haha... they're extremely heavy. Even with all of us, we wouldn't be able to move one.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Not that I'm doubting your skill, but I'd feel terrible if you hurt yourself in the process.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: They were no monsters!
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: I'd like to see us try, haha... they're extremely heavy. Even with all of us, we wouldn't be able to move one.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Not that I'm doubting your skill, but I'd feel terrible if you hurt yourself in the process.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Those were not to be confused with monsters, benefactors. We call them {RUBY_B#Long-Life Curse}mara-struck{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Why have we stopped?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry, Miss. I have a favor to ask, that's all.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Favor...? Count me out. What if we do it wrong and you get your cloud cronies to throw us in jail.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* I shouldn't have doubted you, please accept my apologies. Our road ahead is barricaded, do you see?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The soldiers stationed here must have moved these into a roadblock.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Let's push them aside together?
I'm sure Mr. Yang could clear them out...
Strange, the gate here is supposed to be open.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Someone blocked our way again?
How about we explore the area ahead of us later?
*sigh* I'm getting used to it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh? Now's not the time to turn back or take a detour.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Seems like someone wants to make things difficult for us. Let me see if I can pry it open...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Let [Trailblazer] do it. A bat's not as good as a crowbar, but it's definitely better than your fingers.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Am I a lock picker now?
Prepare to meet your maker, lock!
What, you'd rather leave it to our fox lady here? She'll probably break a nail, and then we'll never hear the end of it...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, yeah, we're watching.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Moving containers, picking locks... Seems like we're doing all the heavy-lifting just so Miss Tingyun can enjoy the scenery.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What? Does he look like a crane to you?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If I'm not mistaken, the containers in the Trove of Verdure can be moved around using a control panel.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Anyone... got a license for this thing?
Is this... manual or automatic?
Nice! I'm driving!
Don't fret. All Amicassadors know their way around a starskiff.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I was perfectly calm until she volunteered to help...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't fret. All Amicassadors know their way around a starskiff.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I was perfectly calm until she volunteered to help...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You've already put on quite the show — do you think you'll be able to find and operate the control panel? Should be simple, right?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I was perfectly calm until she volunteered to help...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Right!
Right! So why don't you do it?
I knew it. This will be a breeze for you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Oh, I'm afraid I'm not built for hard labor...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: She sure knows how to boss people around.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We just need to pass through here, take the barge to Starskiff Haven, and we'll be safe.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Y'know, you sound sweet enough, but you were talking about getting us escorted away by your Cloud Knights. If it weren't for Mr. Yang...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You misunderstand. If you were in my shoes right now, wouldn't you want to keep your guard up~?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: True... But we came here to trailblaze, not jailblaze.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You mentioned the Stellaron...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Mr. Yang, look!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It must be the Stellaron — the corrosion has already started to spread... It doesn't look serious yet, but this is a bad sign.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Stellaron-affected worlds we've come into contact with so far were all subjected to prolonged corrosion. In contrast, much like here, the space station had only just begun to be affected when we arrived. It's still the case that not much is known about early-stage corrosion...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Whoa, so we're like doctors diagnosing a patient right now!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], you, me, and Mr. Yang can make up our own team: The Stellaron Medics!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You work for the Sky-Faring Commission, so I assume you're aware of its destructive power.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yes, I am. As an Amicassador, I've been to many planets, and seen my fair share of Stellaron corrosion... *sigh*
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Get ready, and watch your backs.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: *sigh* Finally. Look how many tail hairs I lost on the way. Oh, my beautiful tail...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We had a difficult start, but things got easier. Look, that's the barge I was talking about.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Uh-uh. Just sit back, and relax. All Amicassadors know their way around a starskiff.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Please take your seats, everyone. We'll be off right away.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Decline!?
Why!?
The Stellaron Hunters told us to come here!
The Stellaron Hunters want to use you to take us out!
On behalf of the Sky-Faring Commission, allow me to welcome you to Starskiff Haven.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: On the Xianzhou Luofu, anything relating to aviation, navigation, and trade falls within the scope of the Sky-Faring Commission, which is one of the six commissions of the Luofu. As the biggest port on the ship, Starskiff Haven is governed by the Sky-Faring Commission, too.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You definitely sound like a... what was it again...? Oh, Amicassador! By which I mean — nice speech.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's too kind of you. My job involves ferrying business delegates to and from Starskiff Haven, so I do this kind of introduction all the time.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Anyway, we're safe now. Normally I'd be a good host and take you around. But these are difficult times. Let's head to the Palace of Astrum first and report your arrival to Madam Yukong.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Palace of Astrum?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Is there anything special about what she said?
Coordinates? Converge?
I heard something in the background.
Right there, the tallest building in the city. It's also the headquarters of the Sky-Faring Commission. Let's hurry. We haven't got much time.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: What's the hurry?
We need to take a breather.
Can we talk about it first?
*sigh* I don't mean to rush you, but if Madam Yukong holds me accountable for not getting you over soon enough, I wouldn't want to be around for the consequences...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Sounds scary. I thought you said she was kind-hearted?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We need to make a few preparations before paying a visit to any of the six commissions. Rest assured, Miss Tingyun, we won't go anywhere. If you could inform Madam Yukong of our arrival first, we'll meet you at the palace entrance later.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Very well.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Little miss fox moves at quite the pace — I can't keep up with her. *sigh* I've spent too long on the bench... Let's catch our breath for a while — we can expect a packed schedule ahead.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That Tingyun is a sly one...
That Yukong sounds like a tough lady...
That might be a little harsh, but she does put her own interests first.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: She did the right thing by not trusting us initially — we were an unknown quantity to her. As for the rush... my guess is she's just eager to get us out of her hair and further up the chain.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It'll be alright, we're not trying to stand in her way. We have nothing to hide from her.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We didn't have anything to hide in Belobog, either...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Nice! Let's have a look around the city.
Not so fast...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I need to give you two a heads up first. Our meeting with Madam Yukong won't be without risk. We need to be prepared and take it seriously.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: She is a top Xianzhou leader... Mr. Yang, do you think this could be Belobog all over again...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are you saying that... Madam Yukong is the new Madam Cocolia!?
Let me guess, they're gonna put us up in a hotel first...
No, the Xianzhou Alliance is better than that. But Madam Yukong will definitely have a string of difficult questions for us...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Why did we choose to come to the Xianzhou now? How did we know that the incident is related to a Stellaron? Who leaked their information to us...?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Careless answers mean distrust and potential hostility, which would make things much harder for us.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Aw, crud. One of us is gonna blurt something out or get something wrong, I just know it...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I feel offended.
Mr. Yang should do the talking.
Shouldn't we plan out what we want to say?
Let's just be honest with her.
*sigh* See?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Good idea! We can be his cheerleaders in the background.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Let's not do that.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ugh... But we haven't done anything wrong!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: March is right. If we're too scripted, it'll sound like we're hiding something.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What if she thinks we're with the Stellaron Hunters? Never mind the Alliance, even I don't trust them...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer] is right. If we're too scripted, it'll sound like we're hiding something.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Don't worry. We'll find a way through. Let me do the talking.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh, you're here already? Sorry to keep you waiting. Madam Yukong is expecting you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Are you not coming?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I've brought Madam Helm Master up to speed. It's over to you now~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Yes, Madam.
rows.speaker: Navigation Officer

rows.text: Report the losses to General Jing Yuan and find someone from the Divination Commission. They can't just stand there watching while we deal with this mess...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Greetings, guests from the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Tingyun has informed me of the purpose of your visit. Receiving guests isn't normally one of my responsibilities...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: ...but since you know about the Stellaron and have stated that you want to help the Luofu, I thought I should at least meet you in person...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: ...and politely decline your proposal.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: The Xianzhou Alliance knows what a Stellaron is and is more than capable of handling it ourselves. We have been around for over 8000 years and weathered countless dangers and crises. While the situation is serious, we have more than enough resources to spare. Outsider help is not needed on this occasion.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: You are guests from afar — there is no reason for this matter to concern you... Am I making myself clear?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: From what we've gathered, the influence of the Stellaron can still be contained.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: If we can locate it in time and contain it, it's possible that we can restore any space — and any individuals — affected by the corrosion.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: We have experience in preventing Stellaron disasters, and we've only come here to lend you that experience.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I've said this and I'll say it again: This is an internal affair of the Xianzhou Alliance and there is no need for the Astral Express to get involved. I decided to arrange a meeting with you as a gesture of respect, but my decision is final.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: ...But—
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Never mind, Mr. Yang. If the Xianzhou Alliance say they can handle it, then we're wasting our breath. Let's go.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm afraid that's impossible.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: ...Huh? And what's that supposed to mean?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's only been a few days since the presence of a Stellaron was detected on the Luofu. Starskiff Haven has been under full lockdown — no one has been permitted to leave. How did you come to know of the incident, and what led you to conclude that it was linked to a Stellaron?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I acquired the access history of Starskiff Haven. Not long ago, someone hacked into the system and opened the Jade Gate, before guiding you, the Astral Express, into our territory.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: The hacker was skillful and even taunted us with her seal. Her name is Silver Wolf, a member of the Stellaron Hunters...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: What say you in your defense?
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: You are forbidden from leaving the Sky-Faring Commission until the aforementioned questions have been investigated.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Don't be too harsh, Yukong. If this gets out, the whole galaxy will think the Alliance has forgotten how to treat our guests.
General Jing Yuan—
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: It's very unlikely that the Express has joined forces with the Stellaron Hunters. They are mortal enemies, after all.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Apologies for interrupting your meeting. My name is Jing Yuan — I'm the general of the Cloud Knights here on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: General, this is an internal affair for the Luofu...
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: I fully agree with you, Helm Master Yukong, this is indeed an internal affair.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I am sorry, guests of the Astral Express. It is true that there is a Stellaron on the Luofu, but I'm afraid I cannot accept your kind offer to help resolve the issue. This is a Xianzhou matter, and it is our responsibility to handle it.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...Of course, it would be inappropriate of me to let you return without something to show for it. While I cannot accept your help with regard to the Stellaron, I do have a favor to ask. Please, after you.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: The Astral Express! I must confess that the train's reputation precedes it, such that it is often close to my thoughts. How delightful to come face to face with its passengers!
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Frightfully delightful!
Would that this occasion had come sooner!
...Are you really a general?
It's an honor to meet you, general. May I ask what the favor you spoke of is?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ah, a matter that requires capable people such as yourselves. We captured a member of the Stellaron Hunters a few days ago, who goes by the name of "Blade."
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: During our investigation, the Divination Commission — the department in charge of intelligence processing — intercepted a transmission sent out by his accomplice, Kafka, who has managed to hide aboard the ship. As for where that transmission was destined...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Do you think there's something strange about him?
He seems suspicious...
I thought he was on our side?

I have some knowledge of your relationship with the Stellaron Hunters. The Divination Commission is convinced that you made an alliance with them... I say that's impossible. The crew of the Astral Express are honorable people whose valiant deeds are lauded across the universe. There must have been a misunderstanding.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: As such, I came to the conclusion that the communication must have been an attempt by the Stellaron Hunters to sow dissent between us.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Why would he stop us from investigating the Stellaron?
Why did he ask us to go after Kafka?
Why is he being so kind to us?

We can handle the Stellaron, but it will take time and will require the bulk of the Cloud Knights on the ship. It is this Kafka that concerns me. The longer she stays on the ship, the bigger the threat she will pose.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Since the Stellaron Hunters lured you to our ship, we shall move with the current. You are hereby authorized to do as you deem fit on the Luofu, with the goal of bringing Kafka out of the shadows and under our control.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Doing so would clear the misunderstanding between us, reveal the true intentions of the Stellaron Hunters, and help us understand their connection to the Stellaron burst. What say you, my Astral guests?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...[Trailblazer], what do you think?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Let's move with the current and help out.
Our expedition was focused on the Stellaron...
We don't really have a choice.
If you are able to capture this Stellaron Hunter, the Xianzhou will be indebted to you.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I'm afraid my hands are tied on the matter — this is a diplomatic affair and I have rules to follow. But if you can bring me the Stellaron Hunter and discover her motive for placing a Stellaron on the ship, it would be of great help in resolving the incident.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Of course you do. You can be strangers and simply walk away. But I feel you wish to help the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: The Luofu never fails to reward that which is given.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...Okay.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Wonderful, it's a deal then. I shall notify Yukong that all intel is to be shared with you, and that our best personnel are to aid you in your search.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: If there's anything the Sky-Faring Commission or the Cloud Knights can do for you during your stay, don't hesitate to make it known.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I have heard of you, [Trailblazer]... The Alliance is very interested in the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: About Blade...
About Kafka...
Once we catch the Stellaron Hunter...
Blade is wanted by both the IPC and the Alliance. I'm afraid I cannot comment on his file.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: There are five known members of the Stellaron Hunters. Elio is their leader, but always stays behind the scenes. Most of the operations are led by Kafka.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Had the Divination Commission not intercepted her encrypted transmission, she would have remained undetected for much longer.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Bring her to us.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Kafka is good at controlling the people around her.
Kafka won't say anything.
Hmm, ordinary means may prove futile when it comes to this individual. But the Divination Commission has ways of...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...Haha, don't misunderstand me. The Xianzhou does not engage in torture. Retrieving intel does not necessarily involve the use of violence.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: In any case, you can deliver her directly to us. Once we learn something, I will share every piece of information with you.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I don't have any other questions.

If things go as planned, I would love to find the time to sit with all of you and hear about your experiences among the stars. My responsibilities to the Xianzhou have meant that I haven't had the chance to travel in many years.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: We had heard nothing of the Express for a long time. It is heartening to learn of its continued journey along that starward track.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I have other matters to attend to. Goodbye for now.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: What do you make of this Jing Yuan?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm not asking about that! Although, you're not wrong...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I feel the same. He's much easier to talk to than that Yukong — their attitudes are so different! Maybe that's why she's only a helm master and he's a general...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seeing as the general gave the order, the Sky-Faring Commission will lend you our full support. The Stellaron Hunter investigation is in your hands now. I'll issue you a pass so you can access the facilities around Starskiff Haven.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Don't let her words distract you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Don't let her words distract you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: As for personnel... the skyports are currently all under maintenance, so we're thinly stretched. What I can do is send Tingyun as your guide — she'll take care of you during your stay.
rows.speaker: Yukong

rows.text: Hmm, I think we only scratched the surface of this General Jing Yuan...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I don't know about "strange," but my gut tells me something is off.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh? Care to elaborate?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: He says he doesn't want outsiders getting involved in the Xianzhou's internal affairs, which is understandable.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yes! There's something about this point...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: He wants us to trust him. He took advantage of Yukong's frosty reception to play the good guy.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Theoretically, yes. But something feels off.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ah, that's it! A minor detail, but curious. He avoided talking about Blade!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Since the Cloud Knights have already captured a Stellaron Hunter, why not use him to get to Kafka? Why rely on us?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Xianzhou is reluctant to involve outsiders in the Stellaron disaster, so why is it so keen on letting us capture a Stellaron Hunter?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Could Blade have escaped?
Do you think Jing Yuan lied about the Stellaron?
The Express.
Go on! Where!?
He's using us as bait...
Yes. The only sensible conclusion I can draw is that Blade had already escaped when Jing Yuan spoke to us — provided they even captured him in the first place.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That's right! We've been framed!
Maybe the Stellaron Hunters have other motives...
Therefore, given our connection to Kafka, we represent the only way of luring the Stellaron Hunters in.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That's why he asked for our help... He didn't want to let anyone else find out that Blade had already escaped!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Now that we've figured that out, perhaps we can get closer to the core of what's happening here.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What do I make of it? "The way of heaven is apparent, but the heart of humanity is often deceptive." Are you asking me to divine their true intentions?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: That won't be necessary. The crew has nothing to do with the incident, of that I am almost certain. It isn't their intentions that trouble me. All I want is for them to lure out the one we're after.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Wasn't that my idea, general?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Indeed, your counsel has always been of great help to me. You may use your discretion on the matters ahead of us.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Hmph, why don't you retire early and I use my discretion full-time?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: It is still too soon, unfortunately. If something goes wrong, you'll need a general to take the blame. How could I simply walk away and put you at such risk?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: If you'd brought me that Blade earlier, none of this would've been necessary.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Wait, what are you up to exactly? Jing Yuan, did you... let him escape on purpose!?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Me? I had no idea he might escape! Unlike you, my gaze never travels beyond the horizon. I take full responsibility — the Cloud Knights failed in their duty.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Hmph, I can understand. There's a lot to take care of on the Xianzhou — you were bound to miss something. Thank goodness I'm here...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: On that note, perhaps it's about time you finally nominate me as your successor when the Six Charioteers next convene...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The chat concluded, and Welt shot you a covert gesture. You understand that this is the Crew's own discussion time.
Yes, yes, yes... I have to go now — I'll leave this in your overwhelmingly capable hands, Fu Xuan.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: *sigh* There are three things in the world that I can't seem to rid myself of: The troubles of the Xianzhou, the papers on my desk, and the weeds in my garden.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: General, Diviner Fu wants the general's position for herself. Everyone knows that.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: She is very capable, but her intellect is burdened by a quick temper. I'll retire when she's achieved a better balance.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: This Stellaron thing is easy. Blade escaped, now we gotta go get him. Just say the word and I'll solve this in a flash.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I can understand your impatience, and I know you want to prove yourself. Now is not the time. If you truly wish to become Sword Champion, you shouldn't be running around brandishing your sword at people, especially not a major criminal.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Tsk, you think I'd lose to Blade?
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I'm saying you need to have patience, Yanqing. Governing Xianzhou is different from a sword fight. The only way to build momentum is to work slowly. Besides, we still don't know who's really moving the chess pieces...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: How did it manage to bypass the Sky-Faring Commission's inspections and the Divination Commission's predictions? Where is it now?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I say we bring those two Stellaron Hunters before Diviner Fu — she'll get an answer out of them in no time.
rows.speaker: Yanqing

rows.text: I've asked our friends from the Express to take care of that for us. Worry not, you'll have your moment when the current stalemate is broken.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: You are my most trusted aide, and there are some things that I would only assign to you. Speaking of which, Yanqing...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: *sigh* That boy...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I suppose it is my fault. I should have given him an opportunity already. "A sharp sword can't stay sheathed forever," haha...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: My fear is that this might prove too big a setback, bigger than his exuberance...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: *sigh* Madam Yukong has asked me to look after you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Seems like we were destined to be in each other's company...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Master Diviner, you heard our discussion. What do you make of it?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: The Sky-Faring Commission has reserved rooms for you at the Petrichor Inn. When you finish your business here, how about some tea together?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Thank you so much...
You seem reluctant...
A hotel? Again?
Not at all, though I'd appreciate it if you mention to Madam Yukong that you got a warm reception from me when you next see her. *sigh* Better to be busy than idle, I suppose.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: No, no, though I'd appreciate it if you mention to Madam Yukong that you got a warm reception from me when you next see her. *sigh* Better to be busy than idle, I suppose.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Easy, I know this probably brings back bad memories.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: *yawn* Well, here we are. I feel sleepy already.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The sun hasn't gone down yet.
Ready for a nap? That's not like you, March...
What? But we've done a whole day's work — what's the sun playing at? It felt like we spent the whole day in the Palace of Astrum.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, that's not fair! My eyes are peeled this time — I'll make a run for it the second things go wrong.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Jokes aside, did you see Madam Yukong frown at us? I thought her guards were about to jump out of nowhere and throw us in jail.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* I'd rather deal with monsters than these big shots...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ah! I—I mean... not that Madam Yukong doesn't have her merits, hehe...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry, my lips are sealed~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But as her subordinate, I have to say that it's Madam Yukong's duty to keep her guard up. The Luofu is facing a crisis, and as head of the Sky-Faring Commission, she is responsible for the security of the Xianzhou's customs and borders.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: She's actually a very reasonable old girl in private.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Old girl?
There is something we must take care of before making our next move. As long it remains unresolved, we're at a stalemate. That something is the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Reasonable? Are we thinking of the same person?
They say that many years ago, Madam Yukong was an ace pilot in the Cloud Knights. She was a "work hard, play harder" type, known for her hot temper and incredible skill.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Eventually, she became the head of the entire commission, which required her to learn patience and adopt a meticulous approach to her work.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: In any case, Madam Yukong instructed me to reserve the best rooms at the inn and have all your expenses covered. She wants to extend the full courtesy of the Xianzhou so that all of you enjoy your stay to the fullest~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: She specifically mentioned that if you wish to buy anything at the inn, be it food or otherwise, just let the innkeeper know. The commission will cover the cost.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Say thanks to Madam Yukong for us!
The commission will cover the cost!
Why don't you go back yourself?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's pretty handsome.
Trustworthy.
Suspicious.
That's the friendliest thing I've heard since we arrived!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's much easier to talk to than that Yukong — their attitudes are so different! Maybe that's why she's only a helm master and he's a general...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ahem! S—Seeing as our hosts are so thoughtful, I guess we should help ourselves. Right, Mr. Yang?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: {F#You think everyone's suspicious... though they do say some girls have a sixth sense.}{M#Come on, you think everyone's suspicious...}
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's much easier to talk to than that Yukong — their attitudes are so different! Maybe that's why she's only a helm master and he's a general...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We should focus on our objective first. Seeing as Helm Master Yukong was extremely reluctant to get us involved, am I right to speculate that the Sky-Faring Commission has some leads on the whereabouts of Kafka?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Exactly right. The suspect is extremely cunning. She encrypted her transmission and timed her communication — we couldn't pinpoint her exact location.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But as cunning as she is, the Divination Commission has managed to find something.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Here are the coordinates. It's up to you how to proceed.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Our destinations may differ, but the orbits of the stars will eventually converge. See you later.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: (Text Dan Heng)
(Maybe later)
Precisely.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's the sound of a device.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Ahhhh, which means... what exactly!? This is a starship! There are all kinds of devices making weird noises.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss March, to the untrained ear, these noises may sound the same. But for the craftsmen of the Artisanship Commission, each machine has a different pitch and melody.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The general sent for craftsmen, and they concluded that the sound came from the shipyard facilities in Stargazer Navalia.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Now, get some rest and prepare yourselves for the operation ahead. I look forward to seeing you in action~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: How can I help?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: There's something I want to say.
Any chance Kafka is still at Stargazer Navalia?
That Starwatcher Avenue would be so crowded even with a lockdown... Xianzhou is really a sight to behold.
rows.speaker: Emotional Man

rows.text: It's a pity that we can only admire from afar.
rows.speaker: Melancholic Woman

rows.text: It's all right, it will get better very soon. I'll treat you to a meal when the lockdown is lifted.
rows.speaker: Emotional Man

rows.text: *sigh* I certainly hope so.
rows.speaker: Melancholic Woman

rows.text: *sigh* The dock's been sealed off. Will we be getting our wages?
rows.speaker: Salary-Concerned Freight Handler

rows.text: No idea. I doubt it. The boss probably has no money to pay us, what with this fiasco...
rows.speaker: Livelihood-Concerned Freight Handler

rows.text: If this keeps up, how'll we survive then?
rows.speaker: Salary-Concerned Freight Handler

rows.text: Who knows... *sigh* I wonder when the restrictions will be lifted...
rows.speaker: Livelihood-Concerned Freight Handler

rows.text: *sigh* It's really been a long while since Xianzhou encountered something this serious...
rows.speaker: Worried Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Hm? Are you a traveler? These are unstable times right now. You should not be strolling around in the streets, or you might run into danger... Hey, keep yourself safe!
rows.speaker: Worried Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Hello, I've been assigned to guard the entrance here. You can take another route.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Patroller

rows.text: This place is temporarily closed off. Please use another route.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Patroller

rows.text: Sorry, this place has been sealed off. Please go another way around.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Patroller

rows.text: My apologies, please stay where you are. The situation is complicated, and we currently do not have a clear view of the situation. We have had no choice but to seal this area off.
rows.speaker: Courteous Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: If you have business to attend to, please do it when the situation has settled down. Apologies for any trouble.
rows.speaker: Courteous Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Please find it in your heart to let me through, I'm on urgent business. Please let me through...
rows.speaker: Flustered Man

rows.text: That won't be possible. Please understand. You're not the only one in a rush. Everyone is. How can I make an exception for you?
rows.speaker: Serious but Polite Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Let me through now! I have to sell these goods on the double!
rows.speaker: Anxious Woman

rows.text: Please calm down. Which is more important: Your life, or your deal? Consider this carefully.
rows.speaker: Serious but Polite Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Please let me through. My daughter's waiting for me at home.
rows.speaker: Worried Man

rows.text: I'm sorry. Please understand, the road up ahead has been sealed off...
rows.speaker: Serious but Polite Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Are you a traveler? You should avoid the outdoors and return to your lodging. We Xianzhou Cloud Knights may be able to protect you, but we cannot stress enough the dangers of being outdoors right now.
rows.speaker: Confident Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: In any case, worry not, and don't be afraid! As long as we're around, Xianzhou will surely tide over this crisis.
rows.speaker: Confident Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: Never mind...
Oh? Let's hear it.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Was it raining when Kafka's transmission was intercepted?
Kafka was holding an umbrella in her transmission...
How perceptive. Our wind, clouds, rain, and fog are all artificial. The Realm-Keeping Commission's weather pavilion manages the environmental conditions here.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If Kafka was holding an umbrella, that means she was in an area with artificial rainfall during the transmission.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Still, that doesn't help us much. The ship is huge, with changing conditions across various delves. I'm sure there were showers across many of them at the time.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Impossible to say. It used to be that the Divination Commission could track the access history of all the delves...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But with the arrival of the Stellaron, things have become messy. Some delves even had their entrance marked as the exit.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If I were one of the Stellaron Hunters, I'd be very happy to capitalize on all the chaos. It'd be harder to escape, but easier to blend in.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Let's take advantage of the rest. It won't be easy to track down Kafka the Stellaron Hunter.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh, let's let the Express know how we're doing~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: More importantly, let's see how Dan Heng's doing! Hee-hee, ask him what he's up to — then tell him we're having loads of fun!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Starwatcher Avenue is a bustling sight...
rows.speaker: Emotional Man

rows.text: A pity we can't get through...
rows.speaker: Melancholic Woman

rows.text: It will get better.
rows.speaker: Emotional Man

rows.text: I certainly hope so.
rows.speaker: Melancholic Woman

rows.text: The area's been sealed off... are we still going to get paid...
rows.speaker: Salary-Concerned Freight Handler

rows.text: How am I going to make ends meet...
rows.speaker: Livelihood-Concerned Freight Handler

rows.text: A lockdown has been imposed up ahead! No passage will be permitted!
rows.speaker: Serious but Polite Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: My daughter is waiting for me at home...
rows.speaker: Worried Man

rows.text: I'll lose money on this shipment!
rows.speaker: Anxious Woman

rows.text: Please find it in your heart to let me through...
rows.speaker: Flustered Man

rows.text: Hold! You can't go through here!
rows.speaker: Courteous Cloud Knights Soldier

rows.text: How are things going at the moment?
I'm not very optimistic...
Madam Yukong is tweaking it.
What a hassle for her...
You've been standing here for half an hour. It's rare to see you like this.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I don't know.
Are you worried about those two? Welt is with them. They should be fine.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Bad signal?
Maybe they demolished the base stations?
Himeko, did you keep a copy of the Stellaron Hunters' transmission?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Can I have a look?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not long ago, on the Astral Express...
Not long ago, on the Astral Express...
...Sure.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Not to mention, 45 system hours ago... a Stellaron burst occurred on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: An unexpected calamity... don't you think?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What exactly are you Stellaron Hunters trying to do...? The Xianzhou Alliance aren't us — they won't give you time to explain. Once you draw the attention of {RUBY_B#Lan}The Hunt{RUBY_E#}, you become their prey. The Alliance will hunt you to the end of the universe...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Stop speaking in riddles, Kafka. Say what you have to say.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You want to disembark, Dan Heng? Changed your mind?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Yes.
Well then, Pom-Pom wishes you the best of luck.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: ...It's simple. That Stellaron has nothing to do with us, but the Xianzhou is convinced that we're responsible.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Stop!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Do you know him?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Xianzhou is in danger! ...This man, he—
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If he's on the ship, then Welt, March, and [Trailblazer]... everyone is in grave danger!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is he... connected to that past you want to escape?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I... I can't leave them down there. It's just... I'm afraid my burden has finally caught up with me, and that everyone is about to be drawn in...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is there anyone who doesn't carry around a past burden? She may not remember it, but even a girl as carefree as March has hers.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: We tread on a Path that is hidden from us. The things we see and the trails we blaze all become our baggage. They weigh us down, but they also give us strength to continue the journey.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Try not to dwell on it, Dan Heng.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The Express spends seven standard days at each stop. Its passengers are allowed to do as they deem fit during that time.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Pom-Pom and I are more than capable of looking after the Express.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: If there's something you've got to do, do it now. Better than regretting it further down the line.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: And... you'll come back and travel with us once this is all over, right?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Mm... Pom-Pom understands. Not everything needs to be put into words.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Best of luck.
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Make sure you return before the Express departs...
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: ...and bring Pom-Pom back some local specialties?
rows.speaker: Pom-Pom

rows.text: Can't send the message out...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The network is down, but some functions still work?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Virtually nothing has changed since I left...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...apart from darkness, this place is all that I remember of the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Shattered Cloud Knight armor...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: A conflict with the Cloud Knights? Hm... Not likely, Mr. Yang wouldn't let that happen...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng
