rows.text: Stay where you are — I can handle this.
Emergencies should be dealt with by professionals...
Are you two okay?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Good. I'm Sushang of the Cloud Knights — I was just transferred here from the Yaoqing!
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: (Shake head)
I did tell you to let me handle it. I don't have eyes in the back of my head — what if I accidentally hit you?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: I'm not a Cloud Knight.
Forgive me miss, but you were too busy being hit yourself. It's a good thing I joined the fray.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Ha, I was protecting you more like — it's a Cloud Knight's job to protect others. This area is under martial law, I'm escorting all civilians to safety. Follow me.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: That was some impressive Cloud Knight spearmanship. Which unit are you from?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Huh, okay... You're a civilian then. Come with me!
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Miss Sushang, what exactly has transpired here? In all my trade visits, I've never seen Starskiff Haven in such a state.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: I, uh... I can't comment on that. I was just ordered to rescue the civilians... Actually, I have no idea either. Anyway, you two just need to come with me.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Hey, you're pretty quiet. What's your name? I've got forms to fill out — can't put your name down as blank.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: My name is Dan Heng. I'm a traveler. I'm on my way to meet up with my friends. I appreciate the help, but I can leave the port on my own.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No can do, mister — it's way too late. You won't find anyone at Starskiff Haven. If your friends made it out, then they'll already be in the safe zone. No need to worry, you'll see them when we get there.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Aren't you going to take my name too, miss?
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: You already said it when we were busy fighting. Luo... something... Luocha! Is that right? I remember it.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Let's go! Stay close, you two. Cloud Knight Sushang will guarantee your safety!
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Ah, one more thing — I need you to write your names down later. I don't know too many characters, I might make a mistake...
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Message not sent? Why not?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Long-range communication technology is still improving. Perhaps the presence of the Stellaron is affecting signal transmission.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Doesn't seem like it, everything else is working fine — see?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: In that case, it looks like someone wants to make things difficult for us. Since Kafka's here, I wouldn't be surprised if this turns out to be that Stellaron Hunter hacker girl's handiwork.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh, you've arrived.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Sorry to keep you waiting.
Seems like you're not particularly happy to see us.
No, no, only an extra couple of hours~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Hee-hee, I like your sense of humor, benefactors. Of course I'm happy to see you! When things settle down, I might even get promoted for catching a Stellaron Hunter.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Stargazer Navalia is governed by the Artisanship Commission — it took me a while to sort out our paperwork. I got a sense of the situation on my way back.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Just like at Cloudford, Stargazer Navalia's meridian pin has malfunctioned. The checkpoint there is abandoned and the garrison is scrambling to locate the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: With monsters wreaking havoc and the Knights scattered, Stargazer Navalia has become a perfect place for the suspect to hide out.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: So... we've got a bunch of monsters to deal with, an IPC most-wanted Stellaron Hunter to catch, and we have to do all that on our own without reinforcements... Fair enough, this isn't our first rodeo.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's just what we do every day.
You've caught a Stellaron Hunter before?
Haha, that's the trailblazing life for ya.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I was just making small talk, never mind the details!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wouldn't say you're entirely on your own, hehe... When you're ready, let's get going~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Shall we, my benefactors?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Let's go.
One second.

Now, what's a hunt without a hound? Kafka is still at large, and the Sky-Faring Commission wants this problem to go away. I made a few calls and managed to procure this from the Artisanship Commission — perfect for hunting down suspects.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Awwww he's so CUTE!!!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Uh, ahem, I mean... what can he do exactly? Are we gonna set him loose on Kafka?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes, and no. This is Diting, a bionic dog developed by the Artisanship Commission. He has all the five senses of the foxian race and takes them to another level.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Be it tracks or scent, as long as he uncovers a trace, he'll follow it all the way to the end.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: All we need to do is look for any trace left by Kafka. It doesn't matter how good she is at hiding, Diting will find her.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But before we get started, let's play with his settings a bit and get him ready~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: To begin with, let's set him to scent detection mode~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Tell Diting to follow the scent of my perfume and see what he can do!
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: *sigh* We need to follow these sparkly traces to find Miss Tingyun, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She's not in a hurry, that's for sure. Playing hide-and-seek with us while Kafka's still at large.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The traces... where did they go? Is Diting malfunctioning?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Woof!
rows.speaker: Diting

rows.text: Got it. He says the wind is too strong here at the port, so it's not easy to follow the scent.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: How do you know what he's saying?
That's a lot of words for one bark, don't you think?
That's just the psychic bond between cute girls and cute puppies!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Using the environment to hide her traces... Our girl from the Sky-Faring Commission sure knows how to put up a challenge. Let's look around and see if we can find any other clues.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Or... we could ask around? Look how busy this place is, someone must have seen Miss Tingyun. That's not cheating, right? We're just collecting intel.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Woof! Woof!
rows.speaker: Diting

rows.text: Miss Tingyun must have left us these clues, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Diting should be able to pick up her traces now.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Customers! Take your time, I've got plenty of good stuff here. Lots of nice gift ideas.
rows.speaker: Grocery Store Owner

rows.text: Ahem, if only business were better, perhaps my memory would start to improve... don't you think?
rows.speaker: Grocery Store Owner

rows.text: You just want us to buy your things! This is extortion!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Didn't see her.
rows.speaker: Grocery Store Owner

rows.text: Refund! Immediately!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, I didn't force you to buy anything, did I? I was simply commenting on my memory. And now I remember that I didn't see your foxian lady... I mean, surely you don't want me to make up an answer and point you in the wrong direction?
rows.speaker: Grocery Store Owner

rows.text: (Show Tingyun's photo.)
Not gonna happen!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Then you'll have to pardon my bad memory.
rows.speaker: Grocery Store Owner

rows.text: [Trailblazer], doesn't look like we're gonna get anything from him. Let's go search somewhere else.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh dear. I'm sorry, my friend here appears to have lost touch with reality.
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: Excuse me, any chance you saw a foxian lady pass by?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well that's a heck of a question, miss! I'd say nearly one in every two people passing through Starskiff Haven is foxian. We might have seen the lady you're looking for, but we wouldn't have batted an eyelid.
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: He's not lying. Still, if you describe her a little, maybe it'll jog our memory.
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: She's... foxian?
She's... pretty.
Write that down, write that down!
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: "Pretty?" That's too generic for a foxian. Even if you don't count the ladies, there are plenty of gents that fit that description like a glove...
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: A piece of white name card, with a bird spreading its wings at a corner. The card belongs to Amicassador Tingyun, Head Representative of the intergalactic merchant guild, Whistling Flames.
No doubt this is a tiny clue she left for you. Or maybe there are more of them?
A crumpled up packaging of the tea brand Immortal's Delight.
No Miss Tingyun! You can't throw trash even for leaving behind clues.
A refined pendant of a fan in the shape of a koi, but is left alone in some forgotten corner of the street.
It is said that in the culture of the Xianzhou, "fish" represents affluence. You vaguely recall that you have seen the pattern of fish swimming around each other on the fan of Miss Tingyun.
You picked up an invitation from the Club of the Twenty-Four.
The invitation reads: The Club of the Twenty-Four, consisting of 23 people, is aimed to taste the set menu Virtue and Delight at the Garden of Gourmet every month on the 24.
No wonder, someone has betrayed their club.
As tedious as it is, I'm afraid you'll have to describe her in more detail. Please don't say "two ears, one tail."
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: Someone was here before us?
(Show Tingyun's photo.)
What else is on the menu?
...I can put my hand on my heart and say I remember this fine lady.
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: Have you seen this lady?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Nonsense. I've been stood next to you this whole time and I don't remember anyone like her.
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: Well, I may not have seen her in person, but her beauty feels like a long-lost acquaintance... How wonderful to be reunited with her after so long!
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: Are you two professional time-wasters or something?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Please accept our apologies! Me and my partner do double act comedy in the Sleepless Earl — the teahouse round the corner. As you can probably guess, with all these curfews and lockdowns, we've hardly had an audience the past few days. We figured we'd find a spot on the street and do some rehearsal — just to stop us getting rusty.
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: Then you guys swung by asking for this foxian lady, so we thought we'd give you a bit of improv — free of charge I might add.
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: Stay calm, stay calm! I did see the girl you're looking for. She took a turn from here into Starwatcher Avenue. I'd suggest you head over that way — she might still be there.
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: Did you see a foxian girl pass by here?
(Show Tingyun's photo.)
Yeah! Oh, wait, um... maybe not. Hmm, let me uh... search my memory for a moment...
rows.speaker: Grocery Store Owner

rows.text: Have you seen this lady?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah! Oh, wait, um... maybe not. Hmm, let me uh... search my memory for a moment...
rows.speaker: Grocery Store Owner

rows.text: I find it hard to trust anything you've just said...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: More customers? You're a sight for sore eyes these days. So, what do you have in mind? I'd recommend our prawn crackers.
rows.speaker: Food Stall Owner

rows.text: I'll take it!
Not gonna happen!
Before you leaving the Express, Himeko gave you 100 credits as pocket money. Maybe it's time to spend them.
You swiped to open your phone with trembling hands. You barely know anything about the prices on the Xianzhou. Hope you can still afford it...
A foxian lady. She ordered a songlotus cake and went on her way.
rows.speaker: Food Stall Owner

rows.text: So you know each other! She ordered a tuskpir wrap and went on her way.
rows.speaker: Food Stall Owner

rows.text: Berrypheasant skewers, tuskpir wraps, steamed puffergoat milk... Oh, a foxian lady just ordered a songlotus cake — they're great too.
rows.speaker: Food Stall Owner

rows.text: Hey [Trailblazer], we're not on a food tour, remember?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Do you know where the foxian lady might be now?
She was just here, give me a second... Oh, she was heading towards Stargazer Navalia — that's my guess.
rows.speaker: Food Stall Owner

rows.text: I'm sorry, but this route is closed. We're conducting inspections in accordance with the Cloud Knights patrol ordinance.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Patroller

rows.text: How about we explore the area ahea... I mean, the area ahead is currently under lockdown and inspection. This route is closed for the time being.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Patroller

rows.text: Halt. Under order of the general and to mitigate further risk, Starskiff Haven is under partial lockdown.
rows.speaker: Cloud Knights Patroller

rows.text: You found me~ Diting's quite handy when it comes to tracking, isn't he?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If you pick up traces of Kafka in Stargazer Navalia, just switch him on. Don't let her escape.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Before Diting can start tracking, you'll have to feed him some leads.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If Kafka is hiding in Stargazer Navalia, she'll have left behind traces. Let's spread out and look for them — leave no stone unturned.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I just saw a pretty lady go past...
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: Man, we really came to the right place today.
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: The right place? Really?
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: Doing a crosstalk here during a blockade...
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: Means we get no audience. That's a loss!
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: Now now, that ain't right.
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: The audience might be sparse...
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: But the ladies sure are pretty.
rows.speaker: Forth

rows.text: Shut your pie hole!
rows.speaker: Back'n

rows.text: You want to leave all the fun to us?
Not a lot of people out there could've fought the mara-struck like you did. I'm only a civil servant — I can't imagine what Kafka would do to me if I were caught in the fray...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But Madam Yukong ordered you to...
*sigh* Playing the Madam Yukong card, are we? That's not very heroic now, is it.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Besides, the Madam Helm Master simply asked me to assist you in navigating around Starskiff Haven. It's no different to any other diplomatic mission or delegate reception.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Who'd have thought that Stargazer Navalia might become so quiet. "Long were the nights, when the clangor of hammers rose to meet the stars." ...People used to write poems about the shipwrights here.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The Luofu relies on the starskiffs produced here to transport people and goods. Now that work in the shipyard has stopped, our internal transport and outbound flights might also grind to a halt.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: *yawn* Of course, the silver lining is I don't have to go on as many trips anymore.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You don't seem to worry too much about the Xianzhou, Miss Tingyun.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wouldn't say that — a good businesswoman doesn't wear her heart on her sleeve. Besides, the alliance has weathered plenty of challenges. We can handle this situation.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Just to warn you, if we do run into Kafka, you'll have to do the fighting, benefactors. I'd love to help, but there's very little I can do except cheer you on from the side lines~
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You want to leave all the fun to us?
But Madam Yukong ordered you to...
Not a lot of people out there could've fought the mara-struck like you did. I'm only a civil servant — I can't imagine what Kafka would do to me if I were caught in the fray...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We foxians don't live as long as the Xianzhou locals, but I still want to enjoy the hundred-odd years I've got left. You'd do the same in my shoes, wouldn't you?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: *sigh* Playing the Madam Yukong card, are we? That's not very heroic now, is it.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Besides, the Madam Helm Master simply asked me to assist you in navigating around Starskiff Haven. It's no different to any other diplomatic mission or delegate reception.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I was never much of a fighter, and I'm not one for risking my life either. Getting Diting into your hands is already beyond the realm of my job description.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I'll definitely be putting in a few words next time we meet Yukong...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Understood. We won't put you out of your comfort zone, Miss Tingyun.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: When we run into Kafka, we'll do the fighting — and the capturing for that matter. Thank you for showing us the way.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Before Diting can start tracking, you'll have to feed him some leads.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If Kafka is hiding in Stargazer Navalia, she'll have left behind traces. Let's spread out and look for them — leave no stone unturned.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Shards of a Cloud Knight's weapon. Something really sharp caused this...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: It must have been Kafka! She's got a scary sword.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Immortal's... Delight"?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Immortal's Delight"!?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: This isn't a clue, it's just a brand of tea I like...Two cups a day keeps the tiredness at bay.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I could do with a cup once we're done here...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Haha, milk tea twins!
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Look, Diting found a strange chest... and there's a hand print on it...!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let me see... Slender fingers, but strong. This hand belongs to a killer.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Huh? There's a note here too. "Take your fancy? There's a reward inside~"
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ugh, why do I get the feeling we're not the ones doing the hunting?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It seems like Kafka predicted our every move... Stay alert, all of you. We could be walking into a trap.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What's this? It looks like clay.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Mr. Yang, any idea?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I think it might be shipbuilding material leftover from the assembly line, though I can't tell exactly what the substance is... I don't think it's connected to Kafka.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Is this... anything to do with Kafka?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's a shipwright's soldering gun. I think one of the workers here must have left it behind.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Stay still, benefactors... My instinct tells me something's not right here.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I can't see anything fishy... Did Kafka lay a trap for us? Let's get Diting to investigate.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Woof!
rows.speaker: Diting

rows.text: Stargazer Navalia may have come to a standstill, but the alarms are operational... How did she get through here?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I bet that hacker Kafka pals around with had a hand in it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hee-hee, thanks to little Diting, we didn't have to break and enter.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Woof~
rows.speaker: Diting

rows.text: [Trailblazer], can you watch what you're doing!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Woof! Woof!
rows.speaker: Diting

rows.text: I know, I know, let's go and have a look!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Agh! Is that a grenade? What's that on the side... Huh? It's lipstick...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "A small something for the lost..."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ugh, she's clearly taunting us!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Downy cloud and opalescent moon are set in twain by the seals multitudinous. Neither road nor skiff shall cross the gulf and carry me to thee."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thanks to the {RUBY_B#machine translator}synesthesia beacon{RUBY_E#} I can understand the characters, but I don't get what any of it means... Is this something Kafka left behind?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seems like a love poem to me.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I've been waiting for you.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Of course, I didn't want to make things too difficult, so I spun you a broad web... Wasn't that nice?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: L—Love poem? Quick, put it back!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ah, I know what this is! It's an advertisement for a Home-Use Object Finder.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There are IPC advertisements everywhere. It's about time I got in touch with their trade commissioner.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Where are you going, benefactors?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Our priority now is to find anything that could lead us to Kafka.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Woof! Woof!
rows.speaker: Diting

rows.text: Diting smells something...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What's this...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...A jade seal used by the shipwrights. It opens various passages.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: It looks like someone used it and then destroyed it — possibly Kafka.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: We should have enough clues here to get Diting on the move.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: No time to lose! Let's give him the scent and let him lead the way.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I think we've rounded up all our suspicious clues... but did Kafka leave them behind on accident or on purpose?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: She sure did put a lot of work into this gag, and I think we're the punchline.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ugh. Making us run around like jerks. I bet she's loving this! I can almost hear her whispering: "Come and get me..."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That would be suitably Kafkaesque...
She sure is a Stellaron Hunter...
Ugh, why don't you go and marry her, huh?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't forget, she's on the IPC's most-wanted list — a fugitive that nobody can seem to pin down... and now we've become her prey while she stalks us in the shadows.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Let's go, benefactors, time is of the essence. We must be close.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Another chest, another hand print. Has this woman got nothing better to do?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "A little cheese for the rats in the maze~"
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Rats!? She's playing games with us — I hate her!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The scent... where did it go?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: When the trace of the hunted disappears, the hunter better think twice...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: It might mean the tables have turned.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Kafka!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: These Cloud Knights aren't mara-struck... What did you do to them?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Just a little persuasion to get them to listen to me. But you know all about that already, don't you [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What a hassle, this place is too far for the diviner. See you up ahead.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Quick! Don't let her escape!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: March, not so fast!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So close and yet so far... you'll have to pick up the pace.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Ugh, there's no way through here, we need to think of a way to cut her off!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry about locked doors, benefactors, we can use the conveyor belts.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Welcome, Astral Expressers. Looks like you caught me.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: You're finished, surrender!
You have the right to remain silent...
This was all part of your plan.
Admit it, Kafka. You planned for us to come here.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I didn't plan anything. It was the future. We interfere on countless future possibilities and make the best future a reality.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: You speak too highly of us, Welt. The Stellaron Hunters are merely destiny's slaves.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Best future? Best for who? As if you'd consider anyone but yourself.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If I said "best for the universe," would you believe me? Hehe... Best for me, naturally.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Surrender, and save your explanations for the Xianzhou.
If you want a fight, quit stalling!
I have a lot to ask you...
We're taking you to see the general of the Luofu. You can profess your innocence all you like, but the general will decide your fate.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Oh thanks, but no thanks. I can't stand moving at someone else's pace.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: We don't have much time. If I were you, I'd make a move before it's too late.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Greetings, crew of the Astral Express. This is our first encounter... though given that I have encountered you in foresight, perhaps I should say the second. I am Fu Xuan, master diviner at the Divination Commission and one of the Six Charioteers.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Far-flung friends ought to be received with fine wine, but alas, the heavens, earth, and body are not aligned for such an occasion. You'll allow for a postponement of the usual formalities, I trust? We should begin with the matter at hand.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...What the actual heck is she saying?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She's just showing off with some big and fancy words.
Even my Synesthesia Beacon can't make sense of what she said.
Ahem! If the method of my speech is offensive to you, you need but say.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: We received an assignment from General Jing Yuan to arrest the Stellaron Hunter. Thank you, diviner, for coming to our aid, but we must escort the fugitive to the general.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Inessential. I hold a proclamation from the general here, if you care to see. Upon detaining the Stellaron Hunter, questioning and all further arrangements are to be undertaken by the Divination Commission.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Did the general just spare us a walk with Kafka? I knew he was a good guy~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Understood. However, the general promised that all intel would be shared with us. We have a right to know anything that Kafka divulges.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That guy... Can I go one day without him throwing me under the—
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: We won't make things anymore complicated than they need to be. We just want to listen in on the questioning.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Very well, urgency demands fluidity... The three of you shall accompany me to the Divination Commission.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Can't we do the questioning here? The Stellaron Hunters are slippery, what if she makes a break for it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Here would be better.
We shouldn't delay.
Are you guys up to this?
While I am here, she will not escape. Only the Divination Commission has the methods to make her talk and bring the truth to light.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The time has arrived. We must depart. Please, proceed.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Let's disembark here, benefactors.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...I may live in relative seclusion, but I can recognize my own territory.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Why did you bring us here!? Does this look like the Divination Commission to you!?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...No need to yell, Master Diviner! The Meridian Pin is malfunctioning and I couldn't find the entrance to the delve. I wanted to get us straight to our destination but this is the only place I could dock the starskiff.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Look — "Exalting Sanctum" — this is a safe place. Let's just walk the rest of the way from here.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Hmph.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Our hexagrammatic position is fluctuating between the marsh and water trigrams. The vessel is stranded and the way is blocked...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: I heard the Xianzhou can tell your fortune — is that how they do it? Anyone can count on their fingers...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The connoisseur appreciates the artistry, and the layman enjoys the show.
This must be the "quantum entanglement" you hear about in stories.
You count on your fingers?
Yeah, yeah, yeah — so I'm a layman. Why don't you enlighten me, oh connoisseur?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's been out of fashion for hundreds of Amber Eras!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What's wrong with that? We've got ten fingers, may as well use them!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I just performed some quick divination and the hexagram is consistent with our current predicament. The starskiff cannot take us to the Divination Commission today. Alas, without me in charge to handle the Stellaron crisis, I dare not even imagine the kind of mess the commission must be in.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: It's true — the Divination Commission really can't go a single day without Lady Fu.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's why you have to develop your talent pool — otherwise everything falls apart when you go on vacation...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph, since you are clearly ignorant of the commission's internal affairs, I shall absolve you of your ridiculous remarks. I'm going ahead to make some inquiries. Goodbye.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Wait, we can help.
What about Kafka?
We shall meet again!
You... really are enthusiastic. No wonder Jing Yuan told me to give you errands...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The prisoner must follow me every step of the way. This is Jing Yuan's order.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Um, you might not wanna hear this, but your general gave us his word. We have to be present when you question Kafka.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You think too little of me — my word is my bond! I will stick to my promise even if this delve collapses. That's... very unlikely, by the way.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: To have this prisoner speak, the commission must resort to unconventional means... the nature of which is confidential and cannot be disclosed — forgive me. But I can assure you that the questioning will not begin until you arrive, even if that means wasting precious time.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: I have appointed someone to wait for you in front of Exalting Sanctum Plaza. Once we've consolidated our internal affairs, you will be brought into the Divination Commission. Please be patient.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: O—Okay, we trust you~!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...I think I offended someone again.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She's just annoyed that you won't trust her.
Well, someone had to put her in her place.
You think?
Hey, are you on her side? I just wanted to remind her not to break her promise, that's all.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph, you do it next time — I'm tired of being the villain.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't start!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't take it to heart, March. Miss Fu Xuan seems like a reasonable lady — I'm sure she's not angry with you.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Really? I thought she was pretty icy...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Some people are not what they seem.
I'm sure she's just putting on a tough front.
As icy as Dan Heng?
Hmm... I don't know how to deal with people like that.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Like how you're always pretending to be quiet?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Haha, Dan Heng's not icy. He's nerdy.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Okay, enough chit-chat. I reckon the Divination Commission could be a while — let's take a look around.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yeah! That starskiff was pretty cool, there must be loads of interesting things in Exalting Sanctum.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, fancy seeing you here.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: What does the Divination Commission do?
Will Fu Xuan go back on her word?
Miss Tingyun, are you familiar with this place?
Just taking a stroll...
Hello, I'm here to collect supplies.
Hello, how's the Divination Commission faring?
Thanks for everything you're doing.
*sigh* You never asked what the Sky-Faring Commission does. I suppose not all commissions are created equal...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Anyway, if you must know, the Divination Commission is responsible for gathering intelligence, devising strategies, and performing divination.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Divination? Trial by fortune-telling?
Divination? Isn't that the same as flipping a coin?
Maybe there's more to it? It's not like I would know, I'm a mere Amicassador.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I want to say it's all in a day's work, but I've been here for twelve hours already... When will this end?
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: What does that mean? It's just a picture. Are we supposed to meet someone there?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Maybe there's been a problem?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's like one of those messages a kidnapper sends in a horror movie...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's enough of that. Come on, let's go.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hmmmm...
Hurry up, Qingque! We'll be fossils by the time you're finished.
rows.speaker: Player in the South Seat

rows.text: The Realm-Keeping Commission made an announcement today — Starskiff Haven has been closed off and the Cloud Knights are shutting everything down. We need to enjoy our celestial jade-playing days while they last!
rows.speaker: Player in the East Seat

rows.text: I heard there was a disaster in the Divination Commission's delve? I'm surprised you're in the mood to play right now, Qingque.
rows.speaker: Player in the West Seat

rows.text: *yawn* Celestial jade helps train my concentration. Diviners need to be able to focus.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Even if the sky was gonna collapse on the Divination Commission, the master diviner would be there to hold it up. What she lacks in height, she more than makes up for in stamina.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Anyway, I didn't come here just to play — she ordered me to wait here for our guests. Time is precious! I'm simply multitasking.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: It's the place in the photo alright. Is this... a games parlor!? What kind of problem can they possibly be facing?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ha! Isn't this hand a problem? I have the worst luck...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Hi there! I can tell just by looking at you that you're the Divination Commission's guests.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I know, I know, I'm sorry — I was going to wait for you by the statue, but— Ah— Triplet!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: ...but folks from the Realm-Keeping Commission descended on the area. It's too loud over there now... Pass! Pass!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: ...So I thought to myself, wouldn't it be better to meet somewhere quieter? FOUR OF A KIND!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: ...And wouldn't that be more fun, too? Better to show you the real Exalting Sanctum and introduce you to a true Xianzhou pastime: Celestial jade. Aha...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Victory!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: *sigh* Now that my wish has been fulfilled, there's nothing holding us back. Follow me, honored guests.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Excuse me, {M#fella}{F#miss} — hold on a moment.
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: Don't worry, Diviner Fu seems confident about getting Kafka to talk. If I were you I'd just sit back and watch her do her thing.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Oh no, Xianzhou divination is nothing like the superstitious scams you see elsewhere. It's based on a technology called the jade abacus.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: From navigation to governance, military issues to civil affairs, every decision on the Xianzhou must be reviewed by the Divination Commission to ensure that it can be executed without a hiccup.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Who knows? She tends to make decisions based on the results of her divinations as opposed to what others might be thinking.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If she doesn't want to reveal the commission's secrets, then you have no choice but to wait.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: How come Kafka gets to know their secrets?
But it's okay for a wanted fugitive to find out...?
The general entrusted the master diviner with the interrogation of the fugitive because he has faith in her ability to manage the situation. As one of the Six Charioteers, she is certainly capable.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: [Trailblazer], look! Is that a...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's an ancient tree — we call it the Ambrosial Arbor. It was once the Xianzhou Luofu's prized treasure.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I didn't know the Sky-Faring Commission were history buffs! Not bad, younger generations usually don't know much about it. It's said that the Ambrosial Arbor is an ancient remnant from when the Xianzhou roamed the ether.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: From a distance it looks like half a tree stump, but according to Records of the Early Nation, in its prime, "it wound into the heavens, and from it celestial bodies hung!"
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Meaning...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It means the tree was as tall as the sky and stars hung from its branches.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So how big was it? Bigger than the Express? Bigger than Herta space station? No, that can't be right.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Stars hung from its branches..." Then how did it fit in the Xianzhou!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Why do you think Kafka surrendered at the mere sight of her back in Stargazer Navalia?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Oh? Did you want a tour of Exalting Sanctum? Heh heh...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Those are metaphors! You shouldn't take poetry so literally.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Exactly, let's just say it was bigger than your imagination.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Anyway, it's just a legend. I see this view every day on my way to work — I'm kinda bored of it.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Let's go.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: On the eastern horizon, the arbor stands tall, the candle dragon down below... One day, I'll see that view for myself.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: Hello, are you here for a bit of Exalting Sanctum scenery too?
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: Just passing by.
I'm on my way to the Divination Commission.
That's right.
Sorry to bother you.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: I've heard there are serious incidents unfolding on the Luofu. Communication with the Divination Commission's delve has been severed. For your own safety, I'd suggest you remain here.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: If you do have an important reason to go, then please be extra careful.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: I'm just a doctor — there's not much I can do to assist you. These are medicinal pellets that the Alchemy Commission hands out to field doctors — you might find them useful in an emergency. Take them.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: In that case, would you mind describing it to me?
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: ...You mean you can't see it yourself?
Precisely. I've been without sight since the day I was born.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: My other senses make up for that fact to some extent — they're as strong as anyone else's.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: I can hear the sounds of people on the wind, smell the moisture from the rain clouds of the Artisanship Commission, feel the delicate texture of the yule flower's petals. All I lack is a window on the world...
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: I've been here many times in my life, but the scenery can never fully reveal itself to me.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: That's why I'd love you to describe it to me.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: I'm so sorry, but I have something important to attend to.
Sorry to bother you.
rows.speaker: Dan Shu

rows.text: The last time I came here on a Starskiff was... let me think... about 20 years ago now. I've been on the road for so long that I've started to forget the sights and sounds of the Xianzhou...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: All I remember is that this is a good place to while away the days~ Still, many delves have changed beyond recognition since the arrival of the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: If you're bored, you could go and find the messenger from the Divination Commission.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: When we confronted Kafka, she seemed certain that Fu Xuan would show up...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: She read the "script" in advance.
It's like someone told her it would happen.
Like a fated encounter.
That's a romantic way of putting it, but I suspect the reality could be more sinister...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The leader of the Stellaron Hunters is called Elio. No one knows who he is or what he looks like — only that the Interastral Peace Corporation calls him "Destiny's Slave."
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's said that he has the power to foresee "possibilities." According to Herta, the corporation believes Elio can see the temporal branching of infinite possibilities — which is very much like being able to predict the future...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...in fact, it may even be superior. If the rumors are true, every seemingly meaningless action taken by the Stellaron Hunters may actually be a choice based on those "possibilities."
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...which would include what they did to you, [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'm different. I have free will.
Is that all I am — a future variable?
Whatever, I only care about the present.
I think that may be why the Stellaron Hunters won't leave you alone.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Be careful, [Trailblazer]. Every time a Stellaron Hunter appears, their objective may be to steer the direction of the future.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: For the sake of this discussion? Yes, I think so. But, [Trailblazer]... who isn't?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: All of us are future variables, our choices solidifying reality. The future is nothing incredible either — just a fog waiting for us to make a decision.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That's good, [Trailblazer], but be careful — maybe the Stellaron Hunters showing up is a sign that they're trying to change the future...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Back to the matter at hand — Kafka...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Her surrender seemed odd...
She didn't resist at all...
It was all within her expectations.
Yes. It's strange for a fugitive to give themselves up, but a fugitive who can see the future? For her, perhaps that was the way it was always going to be...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...but is she really as calm as she seems? The future holds almost infinite possibilities, after all. I suspect she has proof that she has nothing to do with the Stellaron crisis.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Or perhaps something is supposed to transpire during the Divination Commission's interrogation — something that would allow her a window of escape...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: *sigh* Why did the Stellaron Hunters go to such lengths to bring us here? What is the future that Destiny's Slave sees behind this course of action?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: "...the nature of which is confidential and cannot be disclosed..." Is that a Xianzhou motto or something? First the Sky-Faring Commission, now the Divination Commission — they're all so secretive! The general's the only friendly face here.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I hate to admit it, but I'm even starting to miss Sampo... Hold up! I must be losing my mind. Nope — I'll take the Xianzhou over that blue-haired bore any day...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* We've gone from being chased through every street in Belobog, to waiting on every corner in the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Chasing and waiting — maybe that's what life's all about...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wow, when did you become a poet?
Does the Xianzhou scenery seem familiar to you?
Come on! Let's go take a stroll and clear your head.
Hmph, I'm not just a pretty face, y'know! I've got poetry on standby 24/7.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Are you wondering if the Xianzhou is my homeworld?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No, I'm not getting any flashbacks. Please — do I look Xianzhouish to you? You must be thinking of Dan Heng.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Good idea, let's go!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wait a minute — clear my head of what!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the plaza...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...but I can't see anyone waiting for us. Should we look around?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I get it — you think because I'm small I must be a runaway child.
rows.speaker: Bailu

rows.text: Ha, do you have any idea how many people on the Luofu are waiting for an appointment with me? You should count this as a blessing!
rows.speaker: Bailu

rows.text: Our little miracle worker here seems very different from everyone else around — don't you think Mr. Yang?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: So this is the Vidyadhara, I've only ever read about them. They're known as the dragon race... not hard to see why.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That was terrifying, thank goodness the Vidyadhara dragon lady was saved...
rows.speaker: Exalting Sanctum Resident

rows.text: Yes, that child's usually hidden away. What's she doing out here?
rows.speaker: Exalting Sanctum Resident

rows.text: I heard the Knights affected by the evil are going berserk!
rows.speaker: Exalting Sanctum Resident

rows.text: Don't scare yourself — the Alchemy Commission's dragon lady can cure anything.
rows.speaker: Exalting Sanctum Resident

rows.text: Hurry, find beds for the patients from the other delves and stabilize them.
rows.speaker: Jinwen

rows.text: Remember to minimize contact — we don't want your people to succumb to the same evil...
rows.speaker: Jinwen

rows.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah, the Realm-Keeping Commission is out in full strength — what about the Alchemy Commission? Why are there so few of you here?
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: Do you mean "out in full force"?
rows.speaker: Jinwen

rows.text: Welt is deep in thought...
Hey, missy, does this look like a classroom to you? Concentrate on treating the patients!
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: Tsk, what's that supposed to mean? Doctors don't give up that easily!
rows.speaker: Jingyan

rows.text: What else am I supposed to do? The route back to the Alchemy Commission has disappeared, and we're in the field without the right medicine or supplies.
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Besides, we have no record of this disease at all. These symptoms are consistent with someone about to be stricken with mara.
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: According to his medical record, this man is barely over 200 years old — he only just joined the Cloud Knights. How can he possibly be mara-struck? Why don't you... take another look.
rows.speaker: Jingyan

rows.text: If it goes on like this, the judges of the Ten-Lords Commission will have to come out and clean up this mess.
rows.speaker: Jingyan

rows.text: Tsk, when it rains, it pours. The Artisanship Commission has its own issues — sounds serious too! Go and inform the Cloud Knights — see if you can...
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Oh, my apologies. I'm an orderly from the Realm-Keeping Commission. Judging by your dress, you must be visitors to the Luofu?
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Yes.
I'm a guest — the general invited me.
Sorry, the Xianzhou is currently caught in... unusual circumstances. But the Cloud Knights will resolve the issues as soon as possible.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: For safety reasons, please stay in your residence and refrain from going out for the time being.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: And I'm a civil servant — the general hired me.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Technically speaking, every traveler aboard the Luofu is a guest of the general.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: If the port is still open, I would suggest you take a boat to Starskiff Haven right away, though I heard the route may have been temporarily suspended...
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Oh, that reminds me... I have a friend with a starskiff and a travel permit — he could help you and your friends get over quickly. The price is fair and negotiable. What do you think?
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: No need, I have a vessel picking me up.
No, thanks.
Well now, you must be quite special! Don't spread this around, but this isn't some small-scale maintenance drill. The general has sent the Cloud Knights to check for hidden dangers.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: You may not need it right now, but if there's any help I can give you, come to me any time.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Hmph, very well. I still have business to attend to. If you change your mind, come to me any time.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Everyone, please remain calm. This is an announcement from the Realm-Keeping Commission General Bureau. Exalting Sanctum is temporarily closing its borders and navigation routes. The details will be outlined in the official bulletin sent to your jade abacus soon.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: If you feel unwell, please report to the Realm-Keeping Commission as soon as possible. We have doctors from the Alchemy Commission here who will see you free of charge.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: Oh, we will also be distributing a bag of protein rice and emergency medicine to each of you. You can collect the supplies from me in person, or the commission can deliver them to your door.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: Please register with your jade abacus bracelet... Oh, you must be an outsider.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: I see. Please, sign here.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: I heard there's a problem with the meridian pin.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: Some diviners and stargazers managed to escape the delve. Many of them were terrified — they were muttering about "plants" and "roots..." Something terrible must have happened there.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: That's... the best I can do...
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Do you have friends trapped in the delve? If you're worried about them, find a diviner and see if they can tell you what happened.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: This is an announcement from the Realm-Keeping Commission General Bureau. Exalting Sanctum is temporarily closing its borders...
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: Wait a minute, I already issued you with supplies... You won't fool the Realm-Keeping Commission that easily.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: Huh, now I'm getting déjà vu...
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: ...I think I need to take a break.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: It was only thanks to your help earlier that the dragon lady and those Exalting Sanctum residents got away unscathed.
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: Dragon lady?
Our help?
The dragon lady of the Alchemy Commission — Lady Bailu.
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: You mean the child? She's starting to sound like a big shot.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Can I help you with anything?
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: Hello, I'm here to collect supplies.
Thanks for everything you're doing.
Please register with your...
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: You don't remember? You dealt with those mara-struck knights in the nick of time — I saw it all.
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: All in a day's work, although I've been standing here for twelve hours now... I just want this to be over.
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: A friend in the Sky-Faring Commission told me the general commissioned guests to deal with the troubles on the Luofu. You must be the guests.
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: If you don't mind, I hope you can take the time to come to the Realm-Keeping Commission. I'd like to talk to you about the issues Exalting Sanctum is currently facing.
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: I must apologize for your long wait, honored guests.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: It wasn't too long. Seeing your enthusiasm for this "celestial jade" game has stoked my curiosity.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Haha, I'm glad to hear it — you clearly have excellent taste! If you're interested I can show you how to play — it's great fun.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Sure!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mr. Yang! Is this really the best time?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The route is temporarily closed
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: We will be distributing supplies to everyone
rows.speaker: Songyan

rows.text: I... I tried my best
rows.speaker: Yuluo

rows.text: Don't be ridiculous!
rows.speaker: Jingyan

rows.text: I need to focus on healing
rows.speaker: Bailu

rows.text: I can't be distracted
rows.speaker: Bailu

rows.text: Where are the people from the Alchemy Commission?
rows.speaker: Dahao

rows.text: The delve is closed off
rows.speaker: Jinwen

rows.text: Everyone we can mobilize is here
rows.speaker: Jinwen

rows.text: We're almost there everyone, stay close.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: What does that mean? It's just a picture. Are we supposed to meet someone there?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's like one of those messages a kidnapper sends in a horror movie...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's enough of that. Come on, let's go.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hurry up, Qingque! We'll be fossils by the time you're finished.
rows.speaker: Player in the South Seat

rows.text: I heard there was a disaster in the Divination Commission's delve? I'm surprised you're in the mood to play right now, Qingque.
rows.speaker: Player in the West Seat

rows.text: Even if the sky was gonna collapse on the Divination Commission, the master diviner would be there to hold it up. What she lacks in height, she more than makes up for in stamina.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Anyway, I didn't come here just to play — she ordered me to wait here for our guests. Time is precious! I'm simply multitasking.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: It's the place in the photo alright. Is this... a games parlor!? What kind of problem can they possibly be facing?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ha! Isn't this hand a problem? I have the worst luck...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: It's an ancient tree — we call it the Ambrosial Arbor. It was once the Xianzhou Luofu's prized treasure.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Hi there! I can tell just by looking at you that you're the Divination Commission's guests.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Did you bring us here just for this?
Do you even know how long we've been waiting!?
You don't want the master diviner to know you've been slacking off, do you?
I know, I know, I'm sorry — I was going to wait for you by the statue, but— Ah— Triplet!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: ...but folks from the Realm-Keeping Commission descended on the area. It's too loud over there now... Pass! Pass!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Technically, any tree in the spaceship fits this description.
...So I thought to myself, wouldn't it be better to meet somewhere quieter? FOUR OF A KIND!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: It sounds like an unimaginably magnificent tree.
...And wouldn't that be more fun, too? Better to show you the real Exalting Sanctum and introduce you to a true Xianzhou pastime: Celestial jade. Aha...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Victory!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: *sigh* Now that my wish has been fulfilled, there's nothing holding us back. Follow me, honored guests.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I must apologize for your long wait, honored guests.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: It wasn't too long. Seeing your enthusiasm for this "celestial jade" game has stoked my curiosity.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Haha, I'm glad to hear it — you clearly have excellent taste! If you're interested I can show you how to play — it's great fun.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Sure!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Mr. Yang! Is this really the best time?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], look! Is that a...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did you bring us here just for this?

I didn't know the Sky-Faring Commission were history buffs! Not bad, younger generations usually don't know much about it. It's said that the Ambrosial Arbor is an ancient remnant from when the Xianzhou roamed the ether.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Do you even know how long we've been waiting!?
You don't want the master diviner to know you've been slacking off, do you?
From a distance it looks like half a tree stump, but according to Records of the Early Nation, in its prime, "it wound into the heavens, and from it celestial bodies hung!"
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Meaning...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It means the tree was as tall as the sky and stars hung from its branches.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So how big was it? Bigger than the Express? Bigger than Herta space station? No, that can't be right.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Stars hung from its branches..." Then how did it fit in the Xianzhou!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Technically, any tree in the spaceship fits this description.
It sounds like an unimaginably magnificent tree.
Those are metaphors! You shouldn't take poetry so literally.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Exactly, let's just say it was bigger than your imagination.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Anyway, it's just a legend. I see this view every day on my way to work — I'm kinda bored of it.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Let's go.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: We're almost there everyone, stay close.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Just a heads up — please don't go running off once we're inside.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: You may be the master diviner's guests, but she hates people who don't abide by rules and regulations, oh — and people who ask too many questions, not to mention... *sigh* Please don't push her buttons.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: We're just here for the questioning. We'll leave as soon as it's over.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...So strange.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Let me guess, the gate isn't working?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I don't understand, it's never been locked before... And no one told me to take a key.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Hey! I know the food here sucks but that's no reason to shut the gate on our guests!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Are you really from the Divination Commission?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Is it possible you were... fired?
Maybe something happened inside?
No way — she's already demoted me to managing the repository. What else does she want from me?
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Don't scare me! Master diviner wouldn't let anything bad happen on her watch.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: There's no need to panic, okay? This isn't the only entrance into the Divination Commission. I know an emergency access.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Ugh, this Stellaron corrosion... what's going on?
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Great, this gate won't open either. We've kept the master diviner waiting — no doubt she'll blame "unreliable Qingque" for messing up once again...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I knew I'd offended that diviner — that's why she sent this girl to help us!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss Qingque, if you don't mind, may I take a look?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Huh? Oh, uh... no need. Actually I was just being polite, I don't see why not.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Let me show you — this thing is pretty fun.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I'm sorry, the Cloud Knights have orders from the master diviner to secure the commission's safety. The area up ahead is temporarily closed.
rows.speaker: On-Duty Cloud Knight

rows.text: ...Me? Have we met?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No, I meant Qingque. I didn't expect to see her here during work hours.
rows.speaker: Mingyue

rows.text: That's unfair — I'm working hard! Look, these are the guests the master diviner wants to meet.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: For... us?
You're lying.
(Remain Silent)
What is this future you're talking about?
You're lying.
Why are you helping me?
Are you talking about us this time?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes! The master diviner rarely allows outsiders — she likes her peace and quiet.
rows.speaker: Mingyue

rows.text: If you want to see the master diviner, head straight to the Matrix of Prescience.
rows.speaker: Mingyue

rows.text: They're short of hands — the master diviner is run off her feet and the Cloud Knights stationed there are driving away evil spirits. I don't know when they'll be done.
rows.speaker: Mingyue

rows.text: This is the Matrix of Prescience — a large-scale jade abacus calculation terminal. It's the pride and joy of the Divination Commission.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: We've heard the term "jade abacus" a few times now. Would you mind explaining what it is, Miss Qingque?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: A jade abacus is just... a jade abacus!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Eh-he, that's a good question, Mr. Yang — it might take me a minute to give you an answer. Let me think...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: The book Glimpses Into the Beyond describes it as "living jade engraved with symbols for divination into the unknown."
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Just like engraving a seal, the craftsmen of the Xianzhou Artisanship Commission carve faint symbols into pieces of jade, and then insert them into machines to get them to operate according to a certain intention.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Some jade abacuses are small enough to fit inside bracelets and jewelry. We put the bigger ones into instruments of calculation so we can simulate the future and learn from the past.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Take the Matrix of Prescience here as an example. As long as sufficient information is provided, it can answer questions on anything — from the evolution of natural phenomena to the metabolism of living things.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: They say the theory behind the symbols was handed down by Nous, the Wisdomwalker. The principles are so profound that in the Divination Commission only the master diviner truly understands them.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: So they're computers?
So they're just microchips?
Seems like it, but "jade abacus" does sound a lot better.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Besides, ordinary computers don't have cool backstories. Technology handed down from Nous, huh...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Even in Madam Herta's space station, I never saw anything related to Nous.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It sounds like similar technology. Maybe we'll get a better understanding if we see the manufacturing process with our own eyes.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I'm afraid that's impossible — the Artisanship Commission's Hall of Jadeology keeps a close watch over the jade carving process.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: But if you're interested, there's a shop selling jade abacus jewelry in Starskiff Haven — I can show you around when I'm free.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Did you hear that, [Trailblazer]? She said she's taking Mr. Yang jewelry shopping. Hehe, that'll be interesting.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Anyway, don't dwell on names. As long as the machine works, what does it matter whether it's a "jade abacus" or a "computer"?
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Just like today — would it have mattered if "Baique" had brought you here instead of Qingque? It makes no difference at all.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: We're almost at the Matrix of Prescience core. The master diviner should be waiting.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Diviner Fu, how are things progressing?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: We're fluctuating between the heaven and thunder trigrams. A step forward bridges no distance hence.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...And for those who don't speak Fu Xuan?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Ahem... it's an {RUBY_B#Great Woe}utter disaster{RUBY_E#}. How's that for a Divination Commission fortune?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The Matrix of Prescience has stopped operating and the symbols have dimmed. There are Stellaron spirits wreaking havoc inside the commission and the Cloud Knights are struggling to protect civilians. I want to restore the Matrix of Prescience but I have no forces available.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: And on top of all that, General, we still have to deal with the Stellaron Hunter you handed to us. If that's not an utter disaster, then I don't know what is.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Haha, but you're Fu Xuan the seer — the boundless omniscient! Bringing luck and avoiding misfortune is your strong suit, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: You don't need to flatter me, General. It's natural for fortune to fluctuate — there's no escaping it.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The Divination Commission simply does its best to uncover the good and the bad and then make the right decisions. We have no magical means to turn the tide.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: And that is precisely why we need you in charge. When it comes to handling clairvoyant Stellaron Hunters, who better than Fu Xuan the seer? As for reinforcements, you didn't think I'd be unprepared, did you?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Look, help has just arrived.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Master Diviner, I've brought you the guests, though... it wasn't your order I received.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: *sigh* So, general... even guests are on the payroll these days?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Well, since they're here already, I may as well make use of them.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Entering the Matrix of Prescience without my permission is a breach of protocol...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: *sigh* ...would be an ungracious thing to say in the present circumstances. I admit, I'm pleasantly surprised to see you here.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Qingque is often unreliable, but she comes through for us when the need arises.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Glad to have us as your errand runners, aren't you?
I thought you were going to have us escorted out.
It's nice to have people I can entrust with difficult matters. I'm not like the general, and you don't even belong to my commission — I certainly won't be bossing you around.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: I was waiting for the Matrix of Prescience to resume operations so that you might gain insight into my divination techniques... *sigh* It was rude of me to keep you waiting so long.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: No need for the formalities, we heard what the general said... If you need something from us, just say the word.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Very well, then I'll keep this brief. The Divination Commission is currently understaffed. I need your help to restart the Matrix of Prescience's base terminals... and eliminate the Stellaron spirits along the way.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Won't we be breaching Xianzhou secrets in the process?
I don't know anything about this Matrix of Prescience.
Yes, but you needn't worry. You have my permission.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Qingque will accompany you. She'll be in charge of restarting the terminal. As for eliminating the spirits...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Psst, [Trailblazer]... I hath divined our future — we're destined to be errand runners forever...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Just say the magic word!
...Wh—What? Which magic word?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: *sigh* The universal one: "please."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ugh... Please!
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Good enough.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Qingque, restarting the base terminals will be your responsibility.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Oh, and forget everything you saw and heard just now.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: It's been a while, my astral guests.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Thanks to you, the Luofu has successfully brought Kafka to justice... I am truly grateful — there hadn't been a single Stellaron Hunter arrest since the Interastral Peace Corporation issued their bounty. Hehe, this is a victory for the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: So, are you guys and the IPC in direct competition?
Let's split this huge bounty 50/50.
You didn't give us the full picture of your plan for Kafka.

How can we compete when our paths diverge? The Alliance has taken an oath to hunt down undying abominations, while the IPC is dedicated to their "preservation." The Alliance and the Corporation occasionally work together, but ultimately, our ways are different.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Still, it's a pleasure for me to be able to say that the Xianzhou has captured a criminal wanted by the IPC, haha.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Still...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Is this really necessary? I said I'd cooperate with you.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Once this is over and the Stellaron curse has been lifted, the Xianzhou will have no more use for Kafka. If you wish to claim the bounty, feel free to take her to the IPC — the Alliance has no interest in the IPC's reward.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Blade, on the other hand, is a wanted criminal for the Xianzhou — he must remain with us.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Fu Xuan's Matrix of Prescience was able to go one step further than Kafka. To maintain the upper hand, I had to keep it a surprise. I hope this hasn't made you doubt my sincerity?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Next time, maybe ease off on the surprises?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hi, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...You haven't changed a bit.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I'm sorry you have to see me in such a sorry state.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Fine, if you prefer. Not friends.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Concerned about me? I'm fine, the Xianzhou is always courteous with its captives.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Really? That's good. I wouldn't want to affect your image of me.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I didn't talk to you on the train because I knew you and I would get to talk alone here. Worth waiting for, don't you think? You seem to have a lot to ask me.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...Elio said he foresaw three questions, but they would be the same in essence. If I were to hear one of them, I would then tell you the objective of this trip in all its detail.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Since you asked one of the three questions, it means everything is going smoothly. Are you ready to hear my answer?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Xianzhou's Stellaron problem is not directly linked to us. But if you look at it from Elio's perspective, you can't say the Stellaron Hunters are completely innocent. We foresaw all this long ago, but chose to remain indifferent until the time was right for us to get involved.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Diviner Fu was surprised because she discovered three truths: One, the Stellaron Hunters are not enemies of the Xianzhou. You know this now, though you refused to believe it.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Two, someone else brought the Stellaron into the Xianzhou and activated it — a result of internal unrest and external aggression. Traitors on the Luofu and enemies from outside want to overthrow the Xianzhou. The master diviner is in a hurry to find the general, presumably to inform him of this fact.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: However, that's all the master diviner knows, because Elio withheld key pieces of information from me. He foresaw the Divination Commission using the Matrix of Prescience against me. To guard against setbacks, he ensured that I knew only what he wanted the Xianzhou Alliance to know in this moment.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: As for number three, even in their wildest dreams, the Xianzhou Alliance could never have guessed it, haha... If the Stellaron Hunters aren't the cause of all this, then why are Bladie and I even here?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...We're here for you.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Sounds ridiculous, doesn't it? It's no wonder Fu Xuan doesn't believe it either. But the Matrix of Prescience doesn't lie. The answer is just that bizarre: The Stellaron Hunters appearing here, Bladie getting arrested, me being lured to the Matrix of Prescience... it was all to bring you, the Astral Express crew, to the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: In the future that Elio chose, the power of The Hunt is indispensable. That's why the Astral Express crew had to come to the Luofu and achieve something important for the Xianzhou. You had to establish a connection with the Alliance...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...and that's why I had to trick you into coming here. I needed you to meet the Luofu's general in person and help him resolve the Stellaron crisis. I needed the Alliance to owe you a favor. That way, in the future, at the most critical moment, the Xianzhou will offer you their help.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What do you think? Surprised? The notorious Stellaron Hunters did all that just to make you a hero of the Xianzhou... Quite the plot twist, don't you think?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Like I said: Elio withheld key pieces of information from me. The future holds endless possibilities. Knowing the right thing at the wrong time could spoil all our hard work.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: There is only one thing I can tell you about the future: In the best and the worst cases, you will eventually have to face Nanook the Destruction. When that time comes, you will need all the help you can get. It will be a brutal struggle of Aeonic proportions...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...proportions that neither you, nor I, nor the Astral Express will ever be able to reach. In the vast majority of futures, that's when destiny ends. But if we follow Elio's plan, there may be a glimmer of hope on the horizon.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...You know, [Trailblazer], even Aeons can be killed.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I promise to be more transparent next time.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: At present, Kafka has no intention of speaking and the Stellaron Hunters' motives remain unknown. We must rely on the power of the Divination Commission to unearth the truth.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: "Unearth the truth..." You mean interrogate Kafka with the Matrix of Prescience?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Precisely, the Matrix of Prescience is the Divination Commission's ultimate weapon. It was originally used to calculate navigation routes and predict future events...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...but the secrets of the Stellaron Hunters cannot remain hidden any longer. I have no choice but to move beyond conventional protocol — we must use divination to ascertain Kafka's intent.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Everything hinges on restoring the Matrix of Prescience, which is why I would like you to help Diviner Fu complete the setup. I am eternally grateful for your assistance.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Let me see, this is the Temporal Terminal.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: "Observes the potential of the temporal plane." They say this terminal is designed to retrieve information related to time.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: That should do it.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: What? You just matched up those symbols. Is that it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The more complex something is, the more important it is to keep it simple. Don't you think?
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: If it's so simple, why didn't your master diviner come and do it herself?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hehe, maybe deep down she just wants to be lazy once in a while — like me!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I will guard the Matrix core. Once we've restarted the three terminals, Kafka's interrogation can commence.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: When we're finished, I'll give you enough time to talk to her.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: What happens when you activate the Matrix of Prescience?
Why not use it to calculate the location of the Stellaron?
What if its calculations are incorrect?
Say no more. Seriously, please don't say anything else.

Once activated, the Matrix of Prescience analyzes all the information contained in the target — Kafka in this case — and transfers anything pertaining to the Xianzhou into the diviner's consciousness.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Every one of us walks a Path, moving ceaselessly through time and space, creating all manner of karma in our wake...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: How are things progressing? I have yet to sense the connection between the three base terminals.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Divination is no mere conjecture. If the parameters are insufficient and uncertainty surrounds the target, then it is like looking for a needle in a galaxy. Do you understand?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Furthermore, interference caused by the Stellaron spirits that infiltrated the Commission has greatly reduced the accuracy of our divination. The margin of error could be as high as 0.2%! I cannot tolerate such inaccuracies in our interpretations.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: So, have you activated the terminals yet? Why is the Matrix of Prescience still unresponsive?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: There is no "what if"! ...Because nothing remains unforeseen.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The Matrix's algorithm is known as "the way of all change" — it accounts for every unpredictability on the Path of all things with uncountable enumerations. When your objects of measure are eras of time and oceans of stars, there are no true variables in the world.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan
