rows.text: ...No more questions! Have you activated the three terminals!?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: What the heck is this? It looks like a walking gate...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Take it easy, there's nothing supernatural on the Xianzhou. It's an aurumaton — it's guarding the Matrix of Prescience. They're stationed at various strategic places.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I feel like it needs a sign saying "mortals forbidden" or something... Are you sure it won't fly into a rage if we walk past it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We're here by order of the master diviner to restart the Matrix of Prescience — friends not foes.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Passage... prohibited...!
rows.speaker: Malfunctioning Aurumaton

rows.text: Ah...! March, you should join the Divination Commission! Q—Quick, do something!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: This must be the Spatial Terminal. They say this terminal is designed to retrieve information related to space. You probably could've guessed that...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Let me guess — time, karma... I bet the next terminal is energy-related!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Darn, the Spatial Terminal. They say this terminal is designed to retrieve information related to space. You probably could've guessed that...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Done, next.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Let me guess — time, space... I bet the next terminal is energy-related!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Darn, the Karma Terminal. They say this terminal is designed to establish causal relationships.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: This must be the Karma Terminal. They say this terminal is designed to establish the causal relationships between objects.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Phew, we did it. All three terminals activated.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Let's go back to the core and report to the master diviner.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Well done, all of you. I can sense the Matrix of Prescience symbols re-illuminating.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Now, to interrogate Kafka. Those of you in the core may feel a few... impacts.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Wow, a rare honor.
rows.speaker: Mingyue

rows.text: Are you ready?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Ready.
Not quite.
A rare honor.
rows.speaker: Mingyue

rows.text: I have no interest in the words of wanted criminals — especially those skilled in the art of manipulation...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...so say what you will — I'm here to witness the divination of the Matrix of Prescience.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The Divination Commission has ways of extracting the truth, and they're far more effective than a conversation.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Then please, Master Diviner, witness my destiny.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I can't believe it...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...But, the Matrix of Prescience cannot be wrong.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: What did you see?
What did you do?
Has Kafka pulled one over on us again?
Kafka has nothing to do with the Stellaron, but you... It's you...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Ha! Absurd! I'd never have thought it...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: What just happened?
Tell us what's going on!
I sense more Fu Xuan riddles on the horizon...
Ask her yourself — take as long as you wish.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: I must report this to the general immediately. Please excuse me!
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...[Trailblazer], you go ask her.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I know you still have many questions for Kafka yourself.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: If there are questions you want Kafka to answer, now's the time.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: There are so many things I want to ask...
Actually, I don't have anything to ask her.
Is there anything you want to know?
Is this what I get? No reward and a bunch of extra work...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: *sigh* The master diviner wants me to restart the Matrix of Prescience's base terminals... and bring you along for the ride.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Your time to shine!
Chance to impress the boss!
I sense a promotion and a raise!
Ugh, I worked so hard on getting transferred to the repository — it's the best place to slack off and be invisible.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Now I actually have career prospects... this is terrible.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: If I screw it up, they might fire me... but if I get it done right, they'll send me more work!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I'm gonna ask more questions next time... I could be playing celestial jade right now.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Then go. We'll stand guard.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You don't want to know about her motives and your past?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: There are many things I want to know — but they can wait.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You go, [Trailblazer]. I don't wanna talk to that woman.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Be careful though. Don't get fooled by her again.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are you kidding? I'm an expert now.
Got it. Fool me twice, shame on me.
Nah, you're the one more likely to get fooled.
Huh, I wouldn't go that far.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Fool you what now? Ugh, stop it, I'm getting Fu Xuan vibes.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ha, I'm the queen of vigilance, thank you very much. I don't trust anyone except Dan Heng, Mr. Yang, Himeko, and you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hi, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...You haven't changed a bit.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I'm sorry you have to see me in such a sorry state.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Don't act like we're friends.
Tsk, when it rains, it pours. The Artisanship Commission has its own issues — sounds serious too! Go and inform the Cloud Knights — see if you can...
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Oh, my apologies. I'm an orderly from the Realm-Keeping Commission. Judging by your dress, you must be visitors to the Luofu?
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Yes.
Sorry, the Xianzhou is currently caught in... unusual circumstances. But the Cloud Knights will resolve the issues as soon as possible.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: I'm a guest — the general invited me.
And I'm a civil servant — the general hired me.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: For safety reasons, please stay in your residence and refrain from going out for the time being.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: If the port is still open, I would suggest you take a boat to Starskiff Haven right away, though I heard the route may have been temporarily suspended...
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Technically speaking, every traveler aboard the Luofu is a guest of the general.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Oh, that reminds me... I have a friend with a starskiff and a travel permit — he could help you and your friends get over quickly. The price is fair and negotiable. What do you think?
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: No need, I have a vessel picking me up.
Well now, you must be quite special! Don't spread this around, but this isn't some small-scale maintenance drill. The general has sent the Cloud Knights to check for hidden dangers.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: No, thanks.
Hmph, very well. I still have business to attend to. If you change your mind, come to me any time.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: You may not need it right now, but if there's any help I can give you, come to me any time.
rows.speaker: Guangda

rows.text: Are you alright? Are you hurt?
You don't look like you're in a sorry state to me...
Fine, if you prefer. Not friends.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Concerned about me? I'm fine, the Xianzhou is always courteous with its captives.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Really? That's good. I wouldn't want to affect your image of me.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I didn't talk to you on the train because I knew you and I would get to talk alone here. Worth waiting for, don't you think? You seem to have a lot to ask me.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What is your objective?
Are you really innocent?
What did Fu Xuan see?
...Elio said he foresaw three questions, but they would be the same in essence. If I were to hear one of them, I would then tell you the objective of this trip in all its detail.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Since you asked one of the three questions, it means everything is going smoothly. Are you ready to hear my answer?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Xianzhou's Stellaron problem is not directly linked to us. But if you look at it from Elio's perspective, you can't say the Stellaron Hunters are completely innocent. We foresaw all this long ago, but chose to remain indifferent until the time was right for us to get involved.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Diviner Fu was surprised because she discovered three truths: One, the Stellaron Hunters are not enemies of the Xianzhou. You know this now, though you refused to believe it.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Two, someone else brought the Stellaron into the Xianzhou and activated it — a result of internal unrest and external aggression. Traitors on the Luofu and enemies from outside want to overthrow the Xianzhou. The master diviner is in a hurry to find the general, presumably to inform him of this fact.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: However, that's all the master diviner knows, because Elio withheld key pieces of information from me. He foresaw the Divination Commission using the Matrix of Prescience against me. To guard against setbacks, he ensured that I knew only what he wanted the Xianzhou Alliance to know in this moment.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: As for number three, even in their wildest dreams, the Xianzhou Alliance could never have guessed it, haha... If the Stellaron Hunters aren't the cause of all this, then why are Bladie and I even here?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...We're here for you.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Sounds ridiculous, doesn't it? It's no wonder Fu Xuan doesn't believe it either. But the Matrix of Prescience doesn't lie. The answer is just that bizarre: The Stellaron Hunters appearing here, Bladie getting arrested, me being lured to the Matrix of Prescience... it was all to bring you, the Astral Express crew, to the Xianzhou.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: In the future that Elio chose, the power of The Hunt is indispensable. That's why the Astral Express crew had to come to the Luofu and achieve something important for the Xianzhou. You had to establish a connection with the Alliance...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...and that's why I had to trick you into coming here. I needed you to meet the Luofu's general in person and help him resolve the Stellaron crisis. I needed the Alliance to owe you a favor. That way, in the future, at the most critical moment, the Xianzhou will offer you their help.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What do you think? Surprised? The notorious Stellaron Hunters did all that just to make you a hero of the Xianzhou... Quite the plot twist, don't you think?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Like I said: Elio withheld key pieces of information from me. The future holds endless possibilities. Knowing the right thing at the wrong time could spoil all our hard work.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: There is only one thing I can tell you about the future: In the best and the worst cases, you will eventually have to face Nanook the Destruction. When that time comes, you will need all the help you can get. It will be a brutal struggle of Aeonic proportions...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...proportions that neither you, nor I, nor the Astral Express will ever be able to reach. In the vast majority of futures, that's when destiny ends. But if we follow Elio's plan, there may be a glimmer of hope on the horizon.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: So your plan is... to kill an Aeon?
Killing an Aeon? Humans don't have that power.
How could an Aeon possibly be killed?
Ha, are you kidding? That's not what we want.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I just want to tell stories from the past: Stories about Aeons that have fallen.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: That's right, it would be impossible for a human...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...but then I didn't bring humans into the picture, did I?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Is it so unthinkable? There are many stories about fallen Aeons.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Long the Permanence, Idrila the Beauty, Ena the Order, Tayzzyronth the Propagation... Akivili the Trailblaze.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: These names were once known all over the universe. Now, THEY've all but disappeared, leaving behind only masterless Paths.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Currently, there are three ways an Aeon can perish known to humanity.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: One: Paths with overlapping concepts will eventually collide, and the broader Path will engulf the narrower one. That's how Ena the Order was assimilated by Xipe the Harmony.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Two: In a war between Aeons, the stronger side will annihilate the weaker one — that's how Tayzzyronth the Propagation fell. Under the guidance of The Hunt, the Xianzhou Alliance travels the universe exterminating "abominations" cultivated by the Abundance...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...so the Xianzhou too are engaged in this process.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Why does the Xianzhou want to kill the Abundance?
How did Tayzzyronth die?
What about Akivili? Did THEY die at the hands of an Aeon?

As far as I know, the predecessors of the Alliance were the Elixir Seekers. They searched for Yaoshi and longed for the blessing of immortality. When they eventually found the Aeon, they received a blessing that did indeed prevent death — the Ambrosial Arbor.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...But immortality turned out to be a curse for the Xianzhou. That's when The Hunt appeared — firing an arrow and felling the Ambrosial Arbor. Ever since, the Alliance has followed The Hunt in pursuit of Yaoshi, erasing the curse of immortality from the universe along the way.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: After the disappearance of Long the Permanence, Tayzzyronth divided the Aeon's Path. In the process, Tayzzyronth became a new Aeon known as the Propagation. My understanding is that Tayzzyronth, or "Imperator Insectorum" to some, didn't last long...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...When the Swarm Disaster began to take hold, Tayzzyronth was attacked and killed by multiple Aeons.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: I don't know. Akivili's disappearance was very mysterious. {RUBY_B#Aeon of Erudition}Nous{RUBY_E#} is probably the only one that can answer that question. After all, {RUBY_B#Title of Nous}Droidhead{RUBY_E#} knows everything.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What do you think, [Trailblazer]? Fascinating stories, no?
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: They're the kind of stories that folks on the straight and narrow would never tell you.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: What about the third way?
Why are you telling me this?
Do you believe all this nonsense?
...Hold on, any minute now.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Aha, it's begun!
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Unless Kafka deceived the Matrix of Prescience...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Stay calm, Diviner Fu, the Matrix of Prescience does not lie. The logic you have laid out concerning Kafka makes sense — it has helped me to fill in another piece of the puzzle.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I agree there is a hostile external force at work on the Luofu. The Stellaron didn't appear out of thin air — someone managed to sneak it onto the ship. As for the culprits behind the Luofu's internal strife, I believe we are dealing with the so-called Disciples of Sanctus Medicus — that shadowy organization of the Denizens of Abundance.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Kafka's revelations confirm my suspicions.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: You... General, when did you have these suspicions?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The moment the planter of the Stellaron revealed themself. The Xianzhou has the blessing of the Reignbow Arbiter — only another Aeon's Emanator would be capable of sneaking onto this ship without my knowing. We are dealing with an external threat.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: The Stellaron corrosion continues to flood into the ship, and yet it bypassed both the Seat of Divine Foresight and The Shackling Prison... there is forethought here — our enemy must have had access to Luofu intelligence for things to unfold in this way. It is evident now...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: What a spectacular view...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That is true even for long-life species
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Ambro... The Ambrosial Arbor is reborn!
How could this happen?
What I heard just now...
Did you see that... that tree?

The Stellaron Hunters aren't the ones behind the curtain... No, as soon as I set eyes on Blade, it was clear to me. But why is he here, and why did he draw the Astral Express? ...That piece of the puzzle still eludes me.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Nevertheless, Lady Fu, your intel means the puzzle is more complete than it was before, haha. These Stellaron Hunters are a captivating group — such lengths to get the Xianzhou and the Express onto the same track. Who would've believed it?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: General, we must retain all urgency! The Ambrosial Arbor...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: It's the Stellaron. No need to search high and low — the traitors have planted it in the Ambrosial Arbor's delve, thereby causing the tree to grow once again. The Disciples of Sanctus Medicus couldn't hold off any longer.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Every crisis is a turning point. A problem is easier to resolve when you know where it lies.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: ...Am I coming up with the plan again?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Of course, I'm sure you have a countermeasure at the ready, Master Diviner.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: From my perspective, convening the Cloud Knights is our immediate priority. We must head into the roots of the Ambrosial Arbor, expel the Stellaron spirits, and prevent the Arbor's resurrection.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Mhmm, as ever the master diviner's omniscia provides the fastest solution. However, sometimes speed is not everything. I have known the Stellaron's location for a while now, so why have I held back our forces?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Meanwhile in the Divination Commission...
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: ...You know, [Trailblazer], even Aeons can be killed.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: General.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Well?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...You're a scoundrel.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Haha, pulling up the grass requires removing the roots. The Disciples of Sanctus Medicus have chosen to make their move now, which means the Cloud Knights have the situation under control and the traitors have run out of patience. Now is the time to capture them all in one fell swoop.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: You've been sitting on that this whole time? How will you justify the losses if something goes wrong, General!?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Please, Lady Fu, I still have forces to deploy.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: We were in need of extra hands, and the Stellaron Hunters were kind enough to bring us together with the Astral Express — how could I look the other way.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Listen up! We've got a situation!
Let me guess, more errands?
That massive tree has suddenly sprung to life!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The general's smiling again — definitely errands...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's my fault. I had higher expectations of the general...
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Please! We can't keep getting them to do everything for us! Since when did we run out of people on the Luofu?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: You... Why are you staring at me?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Do I need to remind you, general, that the Ambrosial Arbor's access point is a closely guarded secret? Allowing outworlders would be—
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: A violation of the rules and regulations. I would like to remind you, Lady Fu, that the Xianzhou comes before its rules and regulations — all the more so in times of crisis.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: As such, I am about to make a decision that runs counter to those rules and regulations. Oh, uh — decisions, plural. Haha, what a rare pleasure.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Lady Fu, I hereby issue you with the military tally — the Cloud Knights will be under your control. You will act in concert with the other forces in the approach to the Ambrosial Arbor through the Alchemy Commission delve.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Under... my control?
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: You've been eager to discover for yourself what it is to be a general, have you not?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: You've never given me the opportunity, and now suddenly... Understood, as you wish.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: As for our Astral friends... I hereby formally welcome you all to join our operation to seal the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Lady Fu will deploy the Cloud Knights, but I would like you to set off in advance. Take a shortcut through the Artisanship Commission and convene with Lady Fu further down the line.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: This is no order, honored guests. I am merely stating what needs to be done, should you wish to help us.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: This is no errand, honored guests. I am merely stating what needs to be done, should you wish to help us.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Understood, understood, worry not — I know how to repay a favor.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: The Xianzhou has met with a dramatic chain of events, and each of you has chosen to stand by us. Your fearlessness moves me.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Nevertheless, the enemy is upon us and time is of the essence — let us not allow monetary affairs to cast a shadow over more pressing matters.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Once catastrophe has been averted, we shall discuss this in greater detail.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: We were in need of extra hands, and extra hands I have provided — no need to thank me.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Miss Tingyun, I would like you to continue to serve as a guide for our Astral friends.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: ...Of course general, I am duty-bound.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The Alchemy Commission and Scalegorge Waterscape delves are adjacent to the Ambrosial Arbor's seal. I'd like you to investigate these places.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: What exactly is the Ambrosial Arbor?
Aren't you happy about the Ambrosial Arbor's resurrection?
You said there were traitors inside the Luofu?
Let's delay no longer. We should be moving.
It is an ancient artifact that was planted on the Xianzhou Luofu by Yaoshi, the Aeon of Abundance. It has the power to shape life and subdue death at will.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: The ancestors of the Luofu people consumed the fruits of the Ambrosial Arbor and gained endless lifespans — thus becoming long-life species.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Sounds like an amazing treasure!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes... it was also the bane of everything to come.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: As outsiders, you are unfamiliar with the history of the Xianzhou. I cannot blame you for asking a question like this. Let me tell you a story.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Long ago, before the Xianzhou took to the skies, our ancestors lived on the surface of a planet. Like all of you, the Xianzhou people at that time were a mortal species with a lifespan of fewer than 100 years.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: There was a time when the ruling emperor could not bear his temporary existence, or the thought of his life's achievements being lost to another after his death. He became fixated on acquiring an elixir of immortality, and focused his power on constructing a fleet of nine ships. These ships would voyage into deep space, where traces of gods were rumored to exist...
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Did he... succeed?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes, and no. He succeeded because, after an arduous journey, the nine ships eventually witnessed the manifestation of a god — Yaoshi's appearance provided for all manner of unfathomable celestial blessings... However, he failed because the fleet has been lost ever since, and has never been able to return to its home planet.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: That doesn't sound so bad. The Xianzhou people went on a great adventure and got what they wanted in the end, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh...? Our ancestors once thought so too, but the miracle of longevity was nothing more than a vain dream.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Take the Luofu, for example — immortality seemed like a beautiful thing. But what followed was population expansion and diminishing resources. In the struggle for survival, the immortals lost their humanity and degenerated into mere beasts.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: After paying the price with blood and tears, the Luofu people finally understood that immortality was not a free blessing, but the beginning of a cruel ordeal.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: In the eras that followed, other beings that had likewise received Yaoshi's blessings repeatedly attacked the Xianzhou in an attempt to take the sacred artifact as their own. Countless atrocities were committed as a result.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Many Xianzhou comrades who were lucky enough to survive the wars became stricken with mara — a condition that immortals are susceptible to.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Had it not been for the enlightenment and protection of the {RUBY_B#Lan}Reignbow Arbiter{RUBY_E#}, the Xianzhou Alliance you see today would never have existed.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: At this point in the story, I assume you understand the disasters that the resurrection of the Ambrosial Arbor might bring about?
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Thousands of years have passed since the Reignbow Arbiter felled the Ambrosial Arbor.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Most in the Xianzhou regard the Arbor as nothing more than the stump of a dead tree... Only those familiar with our history and the ancient texts know of its origin.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Our ancestors placed the stump in full view of the people precisely to make it seem unimportant, but in fact, they sealed it behind layers upon layers of delve enchantment. Even if one travels toward the Ambrosial Arbor, one will never reach it.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Someone brought a Stellaron into the Xianzhou and planted it among the roots of the Ambrosial Arbor. They wish to resurrect it and achieve their hidden goal through external aggression.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: In my opinion, the force that provided the Stellaron and the force that activated it have different objectives.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: I have asked Fu Xuan to open a shortcut to the Divination Commission for you.
rows.speaker: Jing Yuan

rows.text: Orders received, General.
Errands received, General.
Payment, or we go on strike!
*sigh* I thought I might be relieved of my guiding duties once the Divination Commission affair was over...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You've never really seen us as outsiders, huh.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Who would've thought the general would take such a liking to you? I suppose I must accompany you further... Fate can be so unpredictable.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You've never really seen us as outsiders, huh.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Through thick and thin, we're like two peas in a dangerous pod.
This could be your moment to shine for the Sky-Faring Commission.
Are you afraid of the danger, Miss Tingyun?
If there's nothing else, we should get going.
You have quite the sense of humor, benefactors... I've encountered more trouble with you than I have with the merchant fleet in ten years.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I just hope everything is smooth-sailing from now on — please look after me.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I understand. The Luofu is in danger, and members of the six commissions should stand united.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: *sigh* You did save my life at Cloudford... Consider this my returning the favor.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The general said there are traitors aboard the ship.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: But only someone from the six commissions could bring the Stellaron into the Xianzhou undetected, let alone plant it within the Ambrosial Arbor...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: You mean... the general?
You mean... the master diviner?
You mean... Yukong?
I am saying nothing of the sort, just raising a doubt, that's all. Please be careful, benefactors...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Y—You want to leave straight away? Let me pack some things. I'll be right there.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Phew, that was scary. I was having a snack in the repository when the Ambrosial Arbor started to grow — the trunk suddenly shot right up into the sky. So the legends were right all along...
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Such is life, full of surprises. That's why you gotta seize any opportunity to take a break — who knows when trouble will come knocking at your door.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Given what you just saw, you don't seem rattled at all.
Didn't the master diviner give you any work to do?
We've gotta get going.
It'll be fine. Even if the sky collapses, we have the master diviner with us to hold it up. Oh, and now we have the general here too.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: What do subordinates like us have to panic about? Let the big shots worry about the big events. That's the secret to happiness.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: She did — she saw me on her way over. She told me to go to the repository and read up on anything related to the Ambrosial Arbor.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: A simple task like that is only fifteen minutes' work for me.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I heard people say even the general has to watch his manners when asking you for help — pretty impressive! I don't have much to offer you... Uh, here! Take this book. It's the thought that counts!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: I was gonna wait for the master diviner to get off work so I could show you around and teach Mr. Yang how to play celestial jade.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Your kindness is much appreciated, Miss Qingque. As for celestial jade, we'll have to leave it for next time.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: I know, I know, you've got an important task ahead... sorry to keep you. Priorities are priorities.
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: Well then, get back safely. Remember to come find me in Exalting Sanctum!
rows.speaker: Qingque

rows.text: A step forward bridges no distance hence... Ugh, the hexagram was right.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The {RUBY_B#Relic of the Abundance}Ambrosial Arbor{RUBY_E#} was felled thousands of years ago... now it returns to life. The future of Xianzhou is difficult to divine.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: I'm sorry... Kafka escaped.
Are you leading forces into the Alchemy Commission?
Um, I wanna chat with others as well.
I had long anticipated it.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Huh? She's not angry? *sigh* Is there anyone that isn't two steps ahead of us around here?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Pursuing Kafka is a waste of time and effort — The Matrix of Prescience informed me of her innocence. Our priority is the Ambrosial Arbor.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: From the time the Stellaron corrosion began to spread until now, the only reports we've received on the Alchemy Commission have come from alchemists and doctors stationed in other delves.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The Alchemy Commission is where the Xianzhou's medical research and production take place. However, due to its proximity to the Ambrosial Arbor's seal, I'm afraid the Stellaron spirits may have plunged it into a deeper crisis than we first feared.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: To make matters worse, the general suspects there are traitors in the Alchemy Commission. The self-proclaimed Disciples of Sanctus Medicus have been plotting this for a long time — now they're using the location to their advantage. I must take action as soon as possible.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The general wants us to go to the Artisanship Commission...
He really is a delegator at heart, isn't he... There isn't much distance between the Artisanship and Alchemy Commissions — I'm afraid the former is likely also facing imminent catastrophe.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: The starskiff is ready — I will lead the way.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: [Trailblazer], where are you going? The starskiff is ahead of us — follow my lead.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: I still have important tasks from the general to attend to. Go carefully, all of you.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Wait, wait! Master Diviner, can you divine our fortunes for us? Is there anything we need to watch out for?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...No need.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: My omniscia has seen that your journey will be auspicious — everything will proceed smoothly.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: A—Are you sure? You don't need to use a crazy device or do more finger-counting?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm sure it's nothing we can't manage. Let's go!
Well said, [Trailblazer]. Thank you for your assurance, Master Diviner. Onward.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What's the delay? If you're worried about the road ahead, I've already told you — the hexagram indicates an auspicious result.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Don't believe me? Fine. Fate is fickle — better to believe in yourself than look to the sky.
rows.speaker: Fu Xuan

rows.text: Hey, Luocha, you didn't finish telling us about the {RUBY_B#Aeon}Propagation{RUBY_E#}! Keep going — it's interesting. So Aeons can die, huh? Weird, I thought THEY were invincible...
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: There is no true invincibility or immortality in the world — such exaggerations are born of the perspectives of ordinary beings. Nonetheless, ordinary beings could not have orchestrated the fall of the Propagation... That Aeon was slain at the hands of another Aeon.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: ...I don't understand. They're all Aeons, why do they want to fight?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: You... Are you really from the Xianzhou!? Other Aeons aside, surely you must know the story of Lan and Yaoshi? Isn't destroying the Aeon Yaoshi the Alliance's cherished aim?
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Of course, I know! Well, I know a little. My mum made me practice with swords all day — I didn't really go to school...
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: In that case... let's just change the subject. If you don't know about the feud between The Hunt and the Abundance, I'm afraid there's just too much to explain.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Fine, how's this for a subject — what's in the box?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Oh... this one? It's a casket, more commonly known as a coffin. It's for containing the remains of the deceased.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: The deceased... A—Aren't you a merchant?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Yes indeed, this is just part of my job. I was asked to deliver this coffin to the Xianzhou. Ah, I'd quite forgotten — for long-life species, death is probably a distant concept?
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Nope. The Cloud Knights spend a lot of time on the battlefield — death is a common occurrence. It's just, we don't put bodies in boxes — uh — coffins... In Xianzhou, people go to the Hall of Karma in the {RUBY_B#Long-Life Supervisory Authority}Ten-Lords Commission{RUBY_E#} and consecrate the names and jade abacuses of the dead. It's our way of saying goodbye.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: The foxians and the Vidyadhara have their own ceremonies. Foxian soldiers place their dead in Starskiffs and then let them drift out into the stars. They call it "the Verdantia Returning."
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: As for the Vidyadhara, they're... more mysterious. They say that when a Vidyadhara is very old or has a fatal injury, they turn into an egg that looks like a pearl. When the shell breaks, they come out looking young again...
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: My mum calls the Vidyadhara "Long's Scions." When I was young, she told me stories of how the Vidyadhara could turn into dragons. I don't know if that's true...
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: It's true.
Only special Vidyadhara can turn into dragons.
It's just a legend.
What do you know? Silent but deadly speaks.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: ...Your mother is right. The Vidyadhara are Long's Scions. They are descendants of the Aeon of {RUBY_B#Long}Permanence{RUBY_E#}. That was why some, but not all, could turn into dragons.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The power was a rare inheritance, passed down only to those who could successfully complete numerous rites and challenges. For the inheritor, it was hard to say whether it was a blessing or a curse.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...I've heard the story of Long the Permanence and THEIR descendants. Many myths and legends praise the Aeon for a rich and immortal life.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: But for some reason, the Aeon disappeared among the stars without a trace — almost as if THEY had never existed... leaving only THEIR descendants.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Every life has its limit. Even the Aeons are not truly immortal and will eventually reach the end of their lives.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Uh, let me ask you one more question... Do you know the person in the coffin?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Huh... Yes.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Friend?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: No.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: So, uh... a sweetheart?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Haha, miss, whatever gave you that impression? The individual in the coffin is neither friend nor relative — we met only once. By chance, I made someone a promise, and so I have to run this errand.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Let's leave it at that, shall we? I think we've all had enough rest.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: ...mara-struck.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It looks like someone's hurt!
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Wait! Let's think before we act.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Silent but deadly, Luocha, let's charge in together. If we take them out quickly, we can rescue the girl!
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: What happened to "us letting you handle it"?
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: In the meantime...
I—I've only got two hands! Please — I'll wangle you a prize for your bravery or something when it's all over!
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Don't act like we're friends.
Enough, let's go!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Are you alright? Are you hurt?
Miss, are you okay?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: You don't look like you're in a sorry state to me...
...What do you think?
Ah... Sorry, I didn't see any blood, so I thought you were okay... You're a {RUBY_B#cyborg}puppet{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: What is your objective?
My motor is broken — I can't move.
Are you really innocent?
What did Fu Xuan see?
For... us?
You're lying.
(Remain Silent)
Are you a Cloud Knight? ...Good. Take me to the Realm-Keeping Commission.
What is this future you're talking about?
I, ah...
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: You're lying.
Why are you helping me?
The Path of Trailblaze doesn't seem to allow for any "relaxation" either.
I think they call that "complaining from the heart."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Maybe they're here to welcome us?
That's it~! First you arrive out of the blue, then the general recruits you to the cause — it's like the stories where imperial heroes bring salvation to the world.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The Artisanship Commission is full of workshops, buildings, state-of-the-art mechanisms, and craftsmen designing brand-new concepts.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Luocha, silent but deadly, I'm afraid we have to delay things again... This lady is one of the judges of the {RUBY_B#Long-Life Supervisory Authority}Ten-Lords Commission{RUBY_E#}. As a Cloud Knight, I must prioritize her orders.
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: I'm sorry... If I'd known I wouldn't have got you to come with me. You'd probably be there by now if you'd gone by yourself...
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: I happen to have some medical knowledge — perhaps I can treat the young lady's injuries.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: Well, it's just... she's a {RUBY_B#cyborg}puppet{RUBY_E#}. I think we should just take her to the Realm-Keeping Commission?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: Don't worry, Miss Sushang — leave it to me.
rows.speaker: Luocha

rows.text: ...Curious.
rows.speaker: Xueyi

rows.text: H—How... What kind of "medical knowledge" is this!?
rows.speaker: Sushang

rows.text: The {RUBY_B#Aeon}Abundance{RUBY_E#}...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Very good — we no longer need to return to the Realm-Keeping Commission. The mission continues.
rows.speaker: Xueyi

rows.text: As a judge in the employ of the Ten-Lords Commission, I am forbidden from interfering in the affairs of outsiders. However, seeing as you came to my aid, a word of advice: Leave as soon as possible.
rows.speaker: Xueyi

rows.text: I came to address the root of our crisis by arresting a fugitive — a Stellaron Hunter. This villain possesses exceptional swordsmanship and wields a divine weapon — they are extremely dangerous.
rows.speaker: Xueyi

rows.text: If it hadn't been for a strange accident, my wakespan might have been cut short.
rows.speaker: Xueyi

rows.text: Strange... accident?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Come with me.
rows.speaker: Xueyi

rows.text: ...You know, [Trailblazer], even Aeons can be killed.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Huh? Look at all the people gathered here... Not a good day for commuting on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The Artisanship Commission delve should have suspended operations after the Stellaron corrosion began. Why haven't these people taken starskiffs to safety?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Maybe the Artisanship Commission are just more dedicated to their work? The Divination Commission's diviners aren't exactly a hard act to follow...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* At the end of the day, work is work — you need it to live. Y'know March, adults forget what "relaxation" means after a certain age, hehe...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Sounds like you're speaking from experience...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Just speaking from the heart, that's all.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Are any of the Paths in this world easy to tread?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Still, it doesn't look like they're rolling out the red carpet... We might be getting ahead of ourselves.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Periodically stirring up trouble is part of their tradition... entire buildings vanishing into thin air, puppet riots — you get the picture.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: It seems like the craftsmen are too afraid to go in, but they have nowhere to run to either. We should take care, benefactors — something terrible must have happened.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Either way, we'll have to go in. Let's ask around first.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Huh? Look at all the people gathered here... Not a good day for commuting on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The Artisanship Commission delve should have suspended operations after the Stellaron corrosion began. Why haven't these people taken starskiffs to safety?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* At the end of the day, work is work — you need it to live. Y'know March, adults forget what "relaxation" means after a certain age, hehe...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Sounds like you're speaking from experience...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is bad, master, he...
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: I won't be able to graduate at this rate...
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: Who are those four people
rows.speaker: Ziming

rows.text: Who knows?
rows.speaker: Yunche

rows.text: Maybe they are visitors who are fleeing?
rows.speaker: Ziming

rows.text: The result of the augury is woe
rows.speaker: Chengjie

rows.text: Thank fortunes I put up the shifting screen
rows.speaker: Chengjie

rows.text: Just speaking from the heart, that's all.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The Path of Trailblaze doesn't seem to allow for any "relaxation" either.
Maybe they're here to welcome us?
I think they call that "complaining from the heart."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are any of the Paths in this world easy to tread?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: That's it~! First you arrive out of the blue, then the general recruits you to the cause — it's like the stories where imperial heroes bring salvation to the world.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Still, it doesn't look like they're rolling out the red carpet... We might be getting ahead of ourselves.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: The Artisanship Commission is full of workshops, buildings, state-of-the-art mechanisms, and craftsmen designing brand-new concepts.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Periodically stirring up trouble is part of their tradition... entire buildings vanishing into thin air, puppet riots — you get the picture.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: It seems like the craftsmen are too afraid to go in, but they have nowhere to run to either. We should take care, benefactors — something terrible must have happened.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Either way, we'll have to go in. Let's ask around first.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: It's no ordinary tree — the branches felt tough as metal...
rows.speaker: Ziming

rows.text: Yunche, have you ever seen material like that before?
rows.speaker: Ziming

rows.text: What if I have — you gonna go get a sample for me?
rows.speaker: Yunche

rows.text: I was thinking about it, yeah. Isn't it just an ornamental tree?
rows.speaker: Ziming

rows.text: Have you ever seen an ornamental tree move? Have you ever seen one bore through the ground like that?
rows.speaker: Yunche

rows.text: So what if it moves? I just need to run over and saw off a sample. It can't grow faster than I can run, right?
rows.speaker: Ziming

rows.text: Sure, go ahead. Here's a crowbar and a saw! Don't say I didn't warn you when the Cloud Knights have to scrape you off the walls.
rows.speaker: Yunche

rows.text: Well, I... I—I've been feeling a bit under the weather lately. *cough* Yunche, you're the most agile person on the materials team! When it comes to operational efficiency—
rows.speaker: Ziming

rows.text: Under the weather!? How convenient. As for me — I'd rather stay alive, thanks!
rows.speaker: Yunche

rows.text: As expected, the divination was correct.
rows.speaker: Chengjie

rows.text: If I hadn't repaired the Shifting Screen today we'd all have been trapped — we'd be fertilizer by now.
rows.speaker: Chengjie

rows.text: Still, the teleportation range wasn't enough...
rows.speaker: Chengjie

rows.text: Master Gongshu sets up the equipment hastily
Master Gongshu...
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: *gasp* Are you guys Cloud Knights? Are you here to save us?
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: ...Your clothes. *sigh* I knew I was getting ahead of myself — you're just tourists.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: Sorry this crisis came during your trip. *sigh* I'm sorry it came at all...
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: Worry no more. The knight in shining armor is here to the rescue.
Fret not. I'm the cavalry the general sent for.
There comes a time when we all feel sorry...
Yeah, you just need to tell us what the trouble is, hehe~ General Jing Yuan pulled out all the stops to get us here — you can trust us.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...You mean the general invited you? Is that a joke? The Luofu has the Cloud Knights — why would he send outsiders?
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: There's been a serious incident in the Artisanship Commission — nobody's in the mood for jokes, miss.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: You misunderstand, young sir — we genuinely want to help. Can you tell us what happened here?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What are you doing out here?
What happened in there?
Waiting around, that's what. We ran away, it was way too dangerous in there.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: Please, if you plan on living a little longer, don't go in there.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: There's been some kind of botanical disaster — it was like an ornamental tree somewhere suddenly started to grow. There were branches so thick you couldn't put your arms around them! It spread everywhere — the whole Commission is being destroyed.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: I don't get it, the Artisanship Commission focuses on the mechanical — we've got nothing to do with hydroponics or accelerated growth... Where did that thing come from?
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: You should leave.
The worst thing is... my master is still inside!
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: Master Gongshu is the most experienced craftsman in the Artisanship Commission's smelting works — he's in charge of our research project.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: When the incident happened, he dragged me, Ziming, and Yunche to safety... But then he turned around and ran back in.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: I need to wait here for the Cloud Knights so I can tell them to rescue him.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: ...Why did he run back in?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: To save his research data?
Project deadline approaching?
Did none of you try to stop him?
Is research data more important than life?
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: That's not how it works — the research comes first here.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: We didn't have time — we were scrambling for our lives! If I had an extra pair of arms, maybe I could've tried.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: I just heard him shout "It's gone! We lost the furnace!" By the time we realized, he'd already vanished.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: The gate is closed. Just like the metals from which it was forged, it emanates a cold indifference.
*sigh* Another locked gate. Time for the old dilemma — break in or climb over?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A warm reminder, benefactors, that the Artisanship Commission is as important to the Xianzhou as the Divination Commission.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Our law states that trespassing into the Artisanship Commission can result in a prison sentence of between 300 to 500 years... Serious violations may result in exile on a barren planet, thousands of light-years away...
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I'm sure they'll be lenient given the circumstances...
The general sent us here — surely we get a pass?
It's law-breaking time!
Yes, we do. Still, the Artisanship Commission is filled with security mechanisms. Even the general won't be able to save us in time if we get trapped.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: ...You gonna be this enthusiastic when it's jail-sentencing time?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm not trying to scare you — I'm simply suggesting you ask the craftsmen to see if they can provide an insider like Qingque to guide you.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: It seems more than a little reckless to charge in when we don't know what's ahead of us.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Anyway... you said you're here to help us, right?
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: 100%. The general sent us.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Thank heavens! The Creation Furnace is intact.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: You don't have to believe us — the Astral Express doesn't shout about its achievements! We'll look for your master.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: In that case, take this jade seal with you.
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: If you find my master, please bring him out safe and sound! If anything happens to him...
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: Don't worry, young sir. Your master's safety is our—
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: None of us will be able to graduate this year...
rows.speaker: Awei

rows.text: Let's go, I think this conversation's run its course...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Botanical disaster"? It must be the Ambrosial Arbor...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...but what about the "furnace" his master mentioned?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Stellaron facilitated the resurrection of the Ambrosial Arbor...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: The severity of the corrosion becomes worse as it grows.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: *sigh* Look, the roots are coming up through the ground. I'm afraid we've got some gardening work to do.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Upon Commission grounds your feet do tread! Leave from whence you came or soon be dead! Deaaaad!!!
Stay away! If you come any further, I'll not spare you!
Golden Cloud Toad! Illumination Dragonfish! ...Are you alright? Wake up! I raised you like my own flesh and blood...
Did you really have to destroy my little friends? I want compensation!
You didn't want to listen to us! We were here to rescue you and you started a fight for no reason!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are you Master Gongshu?
Are you Awei's teacher?
How do you know my name, child?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Does the reputation of Gongshu Liang, "the smelter extraordinaire," precede one?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: This guy is pretty deluded for a "master..."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph! Did those hopeless brats send you here? It won't work! They abandoned the Commission's precious assets and ran off to save their own little skins!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Even if you rescue me, it won't change anything — all of them will fail their internships!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: ...It's not like that. You're making this too complicated...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We're passing through on our way to the Alchemy Commission at the behest of General Jing Yuan and Diviner Fu. We'd like you to show us the way, Master Gongshu.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: R—Really? The general sent you? Then this must be a mere misunderstanding! Ah — don't worry about those things, easy to fix!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: But there's not much I can do to help! The Artisanship Commission was suddenly taken over by some evil tree demon. It seized our most precious possession — the Creation Furnace!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: It's a dark and powerful entity. The robots... it was like they gained consciousness — they were moving in a circle around it. I fear approaching it is tantamount to suicide!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: But then, I couldn't just run away... knowing what lies sealed in the furnace...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: We're short on time. Where are we going? Who are we fighting?
One good turn deserves another.
I think I know where this one is going...
Haha, I'm sure General Jing Yuan must have believed wholeheartedly that you could save the Artisanship Commission from this crisis.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Means I know of may yet serve your fight, pray you in repayment aid my plight. Come! Come on, through here~
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Look, this is one of the Artisanship Commission's prototypes: The Shifting Screen.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Good thing I got the students to take it out and make a few adjustments — otherwise they'd never have managed to get out in time.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: You all saw the Jade Gate on your way in, I assume? The Shifting Screen works in the same way. It connects two spatial coordinates in ways that laymen, ahem, wouldn't understand.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Like teleportation?
Then what do you need starskiffs for?
Gongshu Liang strikes a pose and raises an eyebrow as if to say: "keep asking."
Indeed. With limited range and energy costs aside, to every starskiff soon shall woe betide~!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: You sure about that? Even our trailblazing Space Anchors sound better.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Thank goodness you take the time to perfect these inventions, master! If not, the Sky-Faring Commission would've become quite redundant by now.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: Ordinarily I could've used this beauty to teleport you thither, but... Through earth and air the wretched branches boiled, the Shifting Screen entangled thence... encoiled!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: I'm sure you know how to fix it.
Thanks for the colorful explanation. Bye!
Then I shall inform the general that this path is a no-go.
How observant — you would make an excellent student.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: H—Hold on! Have some faith in me!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: H—Hold on! My young friends, don't underestimate the Artisanship Commission. The general is too far off to help us now, but I can!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: The Commission is more than a match for mother nature. Hmph! O piteous tree, who think thyself so strong, your match and more in strength to meet ere long...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: This is the first thing that came to mind when the tree demon attacked.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: It's a mechanical device code-named the Luminflux Pyxis.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: I invented this weapon for the Cloud Knights. It's incredibly powerful, but...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Let me guess... Limited range? Energy costs?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Say hello to our very "deer" friend! ...Get it?
Go hoof some fun!
Deer hunting.
Please never do that again...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I feel like I'm gonna be sick...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* Every light has its shadow. But this is more than enough to deal with the tree demon.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: And then, ignite. Fire beats wood — there's no way we can lose!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Very good! The master reveals the door, but the apprentice must walk through it. You're much better than my useless students.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Wh—What's happening? Is the delve collapsing?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Phew, seems like it worked! That tree demon must be writhing in pain, hahaha.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Alright, there's no time to lose. Hurry through the Shifting Screen to the opposite side before the branches grow back.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Look, the Ambrosial Arbor's roots...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: They've encoiled the Artisanship Commission's most precious invention: The Creation Furnace!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Help me, dear young friends! Let's hack them away together! We can't let the roots punch through the furnace!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: No matter how much damage we do, it just heals itself... not fair!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We'll have to retreat for now. Follow me!
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Ugh, no wonder the Xianzhou is so scared of the Abominations of Abundance — they're unstoppable!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Miss Tingyun, are the long-life species on the Xianzhou... all like this?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm afraid this Ebon Deer was likely birthed by the Ambrosial Arbor as its guardian — it shares a close connection with the Arbor's roots. Most living creatures on the Xianzhou don't have abilities like this.
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: *sigh* As long as it's there, we can't get any closer.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wonder... The Ebon Deer seems to heal itself instantly, but perhaps it's drawing that power from elsewhere...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Let's blast it to smithereens!
So if we follow the roots we can find the source of its power?
[Trailblazer], are you listening to Mr. Yang!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah! It can't heal if we take out the source, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The monster only seems to be active in the vicinity of the Arbor. Let's look around and see if we can find anything.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: So the general asked you to head to the Alchemy Commission?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: *sigh* The Artisanship Commission had no choice but to halt operations once the tree demon appeared.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: ...Young friends, I have a suggestion. Why don't we head that way?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Any thoughts, Master Gongshu?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hmm... When the deer revives, the surrounding roots glow brightly...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Great observation Mr. Gongshu. It's amazing what you notice when you're not fighting...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hehe, I'm only an artisan, after all. My skills in clash of swords shall find no sake, yet that which clasheth needeth hands to make!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: As Mr. Yang said, the deer monster is likely drawing power from somewhere in order to replenish itself. I'm certain that when the Arbor glows, we are witnessing that very process.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Maybe the root system is the key.
Let's give it a shot — nothing to lose.
Precisely! You remember how we untangled the Shifting Screen with fire?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: You're right! Those roots never grew back!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Not only that — its reaction suggested we'd hurt it... perhaps that's our starting point.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Take hold of your weapons, young comrades! Let's raze these roots to the ground!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: See!? My theory was correct! Keep going!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Quick, there's more roots over here!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Give me a moment — I'll set up the device.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: I guess we're done...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I suspect the Ambrosial Arbor's root system must have spread far underground. The only thing we can say with confidence is that we removed the majority of those within the bounds of the Artisanship Commission.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Let's hurry, before they've had a chance to grow back.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: So, the next step is...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Let's go!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Look — the roots coiled around the Creation Furnace! They've withered!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Excellent! Nothing can stop you now!
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: General Jing Yuan said the Ambrosial Arbor was an unfathomable celestial blessing...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: At first glance, that deer could have been an ordinary life form, but the ability to heal such grave wounds in an instant... I think I finally understand why the Xianzhou decided to follow The Hunt in eradicating the Abundance.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: If immortal creations were left to spread their branches and roots throughout the universe, entire ecosystems would collapse...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: No wonder the people of the Xianzhou wander the universe, never settling on a planet...
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: You are a man of vision, Mr. Yang. It's a shame our ancestors, the Elixir Seekers, were unable to see that hidden curse 8000 years ago...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Perhaps some of them did reject the {RUBY_B#Yaoshi}Plagues Author{RUBY_E#}'s "gift." But how could an entire civilization resist the temptation of immortality?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Ironic, isn't it? The wise are buried while the fools remain immortal...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: The Xianzhou regrets being led astray by the Abundance... That's why they have decided to embark on the Path of The Hunt. Maybe it's not too late for redemption.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Thank you for your help. I realize you must continue on to the Alchemy Commission, to the Ambrosial Arbor. After witnessing what happened here, I know there will only be more danger ahead.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Go, friends, and stay vigilant. I wish you a safe journey.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Thank you for your help. Those useless students and I will take care of the rest here... If worst comes to worst, we still have the Cloud Knights.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Why do you care so much about this furnace?
Have you heard from the Alchemy Commission delve?
Well then, goodbye.
It's only a legend... though what with the Ambrosial Arbor having come back to life, I suppose it's no longer absurd...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: They say that a long time ago, when the Xianzhou Alliance was adrift in deep space, it encountered many unimaginable life forms.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Among them were abominations known as heliobi. They existed in the form of pure energy, but craved the sensations and desires of mortal flesh and blood. Sometimes they managed to infiltrate the delves of the Xianzhou in order to bewitch humans and become parasites in their bodies.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: It's said that mortals parasitized by heliobi would lose their free will imperceptibly, before gradually going berserk.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: After a prolonged struggle, the people of the Xianzhou finally managed to trap and seal the heliobi in a vessel.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: That vessel is the Creation Furnace. Our predecessors hoped that by burning the heliobi in the furnace, their energy would gradually be exhausted until they were completely destroyed.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: I don't know if there are demons in the furnace — perhaps it's all just superstition. However, from the day I started learning from my master, I've looked after the operation of the furnace.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Indeed, the flame inside has never been extinguished...
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Everything happened so quickly. My students and I were caught by surprise.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: According to the general, there are traitors in the Alchemy Commission.
I heard the Disciples of Sanctus Medicus shut down the Alchemy Commission.
I'm not overly surprised. The Alchemy Commission's alchemists were once closer to the Arbor than anyone else on the Luofu.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: The Disciples of Sanctus Medicus? Now there's an old name.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: They say that when the Xianzhou Luofu was first granted the Ambrosial Arbor, the alchemists in the Alchemy Commission wielded tremendous influence. Using the power of the Arbor, they transformed mortal bodies, manipulated the weather, and even brought never-before-seen creatures into being.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: They called themselves "Saints." Unfortunately, they didn't possess any saintly powers. As soon as the Ambrosial Arbor withered, the alchemists lost their status and were reduced to medical researchers and practitioners.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: I'm sorry I'm not able to accompany you further.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Agh, I've always hated owing a favor. Take these with you — rewards for your tireless efforts.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: It's a whole row of those gate robots! We saw one in the Divination Commission...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Gate robots...? Those are aurumatons — the Artisanship Commission created them to stand guard in various locations.
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu

rows.text: Master, are these creations truly able to protect the Artisanship Commission? There's already been so much destruction — why haven't we seen any in action?
rows.speaker: Tingyun

rows.text: I... Ahem! We haven't quite finished the paintwork on this batch. How can we deploy them if they're not looking their best?
rows.speaker: Master Gongshu
